One of the first things Andy Burnham did on July 20, 2026, after assuming the role of Britain’s prime minister was make a long-distance call to Donald Trump.

The U.S. president later revealed some of the details of his conversation with “the new gentleman,” noting that they discussed “opening up North Sea oil” – a topic seemingly close to Trump’s heart.

But there have as yet been few clues on how Burnham intends to manage the “special relationship” between the U.S. and U.K. Certainly, that task will not have been made easier by the Labour Party leader’s past comments about Trump or those of his foreign secretary, Ed Miliband – a “racist, misogynistic self-confessed groper,” was Britain’s now top diplomat’s assessment of the U.S. leader back in 2016.

As an expert in U.K. politics and trans-Atlantic relations, I know that dealing with Trump will be a foreign policy priority for Burnham.

open image in gallery Andy Burnham hardly inherited a clear path to follow for a post-Brexit Britain ( Reuters )

However, the challenges for the special relationship go beyond navigating personalities. Indeed, the enduring political instability in the U.K. since 2016 and the Brexit referendum that saw the U.K. exit the European Union is spilling over into foreign policy. Leadership turnover is hindering important reforms at home, but it is also preventing the U.K. from developing a clear strategy on the international stage.

Instability here to stay?

The U.K. has experienced a striking leadership carousel in the past decade.

Burnham is the sixth prime minister since David Cameron resigned in the aftermath of the Brexit referendum in June 2016. And the turnover has also applied to other senior government positions. Miliband has become the the ninth foreign secretary over that period.

This pattern of instability is highly unusual from a historical standpoint. Not since the 1820s has there been as many different prime ministers within the span of 10 years. And this past decade also marks a significant deviation from the rest of the post-World War II era – the period in which the special relationship navigated the reconstruction of Europe, the Cold War, the rise of China and threats from international terrorism.

Between 1945 and 2016, U.K. prime ministers averaged five years in power; since then it has dropped to just 24 months.

Post-2016 prime ministers have been ultimately brought down for different reasons, including repeated scandals, poor choices and lost elections.

But in all cases, their leadership was eroded by deep structural forces, especially the impact of Brexit.

Like prime ministers before him, Burnham is inheriting a sluggish economy, in part due to the significant economic costs of exiting the European market. He is also in charge of an economy that is more exposed to Trump’s attacks against the rules-based trading order, while unable to benefit from the shock absorbers provided by the EU’s large internal market.

Domestically, Brexit has deeply polarized the British electorate into new identities – leavers and remainers – who are less loyal to existing political parties. This has led to increased electoral volatility, which has helped to accelerate the fragmentation of British politics. For the first time in a century, there is a strong chance that the next prime minister will not be from one of the two main established parties, Labour and the Conservatives.

About the author Garret Martin is Hurst Senior Professorial Lecturer, Co-Director Transatlantic Policy Center, American University School of International Service. This article was first published by The Conversation and is republished under a Creative Commons licence. Read the original article .

The shift to a more multiparty system has led to more competitive local elections, with more vulnerable seats and members of Parliament elected thanks to very small majorities in their constituencies. This shift has moved in tandem with the growing dynamic of parliamentarians becoming more rebellious and less loyal to their leadership.

In other words, Burnham faces a tall order if he is to put a wedge in the revolving door at No. 10 Downing St., the residence of Britain’s prime minister.

Short-lived tandems

The impact of the prime minister carousel has not been confined to domestic politics – it is difficult to maintain a consistent and coherent foreign policy when those dictating it keep changing. This is particularly meaningful for the special relationship, as Brexit has made the U.K. more dependent on the U.S. Granted, much of the present attention will center on how Burnham manages, or not, his ties with Trump.

But leadership instability has and will continue to present additional challenges for the U.K.-U.S. partnership.

First, while not as drastic as in the U.K., U.S. politics are also experiencing more turnover than usual since 2016. Faith in the U.S. government plummeted to 17% in 2025, with voters increasingly irritable and impatient. This is also translating into greater volatility. At least one chamber of Congress has changed hands every two years since 2018, with the streak likely to continue in the midterms in November. And the succession of three one-term presidents has not happened in over a hundred years.

As a result, leadership ties between the U.S. and the U.K. have failed to build any momentum. In the past decade, the average tandem has barely lasted more than a year. At best, Burnham could coexist with Trump for a little over two years, with much of that including the latter’s lame-duck period.

Unclear post-Brexit strategy

Meanwhile, U.S. statesman Dean Acheson’s famous 1962 quip that “Great Britain has lost an empire and has not yet found a role” still rings true.

Exiting from the EU presented a profound challenge for the U.K. and what role it should play on the international stage. Brexit, after all, undermined Britain’s ability to play the role of bridge between America and Europe.

Yet, Burnham hardly inherited a clear path to follow for a post-Brexit Britain. This is not surprising considering that divided societies are less equipped to maintain a long-term strategy.

open image in gallery There have as yet been few clues on how Burnham intends to manage the ‘special relationship’ between the U.S. and U.K. ( Getty )

Successive leaders after 2016 failed to develop a clear post-Brexit doctrine, relying instead on an ad hoc balancing act between an Atlantic path, more cooperation with European partners and strategic autonomy. That does not bode well for the special relationship, at a time when the U.K. is grappling, like others, with the key dilemma of how to defend Europe without the U.S.

Strong headwinds

If Burnham does want to preserve and bolster the special relationship, he will need time in office to counter the current strong headwinds.

Historically, the partnership between the U.S. and the U.K. has endured testing times and similarly politically mismatched leaders. Burnham is seen as to the left of predecessor Keir Starmer in the center-left Labour Party – some way off Trump’s brand of conservatism. But Tony Blair and George W. Bush overcame divergent political ideologies a generation ago to forge a close relationship.

But back then, the special relationship relied on deeper institutional ties, whether cultural, diplomatic, military or in the field of intelligence. Yet, the impact has been somewhat blunted of late by Trump’s very personalized diplomacy. Trump’s mistrust of the bureaucracy has limited Britain’s ability to benefit from its deep ties with the American foreign policy establishment.

Moreover, Trump’s deep unpopularity in the U.K. – just 13% had a favorable opinion of Trump, compared to 83% who held an unfavorable opinion – is spilling over into perceptions of the special relationship. Increasingly, Britons are viewing the U.S. as a necessary partner, as opposed to an ally with which it shares close values. Such growing disaffection is not a one-way street, with American approval of Britain dropping by 15% in the past five years. It also builds on part of the MAGA base that views the U.K. as in decline and having lost its way.

As such, Burnham has inherited a tall task domestically and internationally. He will have to tackle the same challenges of Brexit that toppled his predecessors while shaping a more coherent post-Brexit future for the U.K. Confronting both would go a long way toward stabilizing the special relationship.

Chicago Fire is losing fan interest as yet another cast member departs the show.

The popular NBC firefighter drama, which is scheduled to return for season 15 in October, is reportedly losing Dermot Mulroney after only two years.

Mulroney, 62, who joined the long-running procedural in 2024 as Battalion Chief Dom Pascal, will officially leave the series early in the new season, according to various publications.

No reason has been given for his departure; however, there is speculation that it may be related to his upcoming role in season two of Netflix’s The Hunting Wives.

The Independent has contacted NBC for comment.

open image in gallery Dermot Mulroney joined 'Chicago Fire' in 2024 as Battalion Chief Dom Pascal ( Elizabeth Sisson/NBC )

open image in gallery News of Mulroney’s departure comes on the heels of original cast member Joe Miñoso’s exit ( Elizabeth Sisson/NBC )

Despite his brief time on the show, Mulroney had grown popular among fans, who have since expressed disappointment over news of his departure.

“Oh! No!! This is too much to handle!! I love Dermot! He did a fabulous job! And he fit the role! I guess he’s doing other things, saw his movie, it was pretty good, I’m upset, I really liked him on the show! Now we have to get used to too many new people,” one person wrote on X.

“Wow that’s surprising!” a second reacted, with a third arguing that the “show should just be canceled at this point.”

“What is even happening over there?!” a fourth questioned, as another demanded, “They need to tell us what’s going on with the show and the whole franchise.”

Several applauded Mulroney’s work on the show. He added “such a [grounding] presence to the station,” one praised, followed by a second who thanked him for everything “he brought to the series.”

open image in gallery Miñoso (right) is leaving the series after 14 years ( NBC )

“With #JoeMinoso also leaving, that firehouse has some serious rebuilding to do,” they added, referencing the recent news that the original Chicago Fire star will also be leaving the show after 14 years.

Miñoso, 47, has played firefighter Joe Cruz since the show’s 2012 debut. He first joined as a guest star in the show’s pilot before being promoted to a series regular at the start of season two. Like Mulroney, he has also appeared on the fellow One Chicago franchise shows Chicago Med and Chicago P.D.

On the show’s Reddit page, a fan similarly lamented the back-to-back casting exits. “First Carver, now Pascal... I understand that in a long-running show, we eventually end up losing some characters and have to accept some kind of rotation because, in the long run, it’s cheaper to hire new actors,” they acknowledged. “But we’re reaching a level where it’s so frustrating. It’s happening too fast. A new character is introduced, and after just a few seasons, once you’ve finally bonded with them, they’re already gone.”

In 2024, Mulroney raved about joining Chicago Fire, telling NBC Insider the experience is “brand new for me.”

“I’m also joining a cast that’s already here. So I’m really the new guy in a brand new experience. I’ve never played a part that will last this long. I’ve never worked on a job for this many months as our filming schedule rolls over into 2025,” the Anyone But You actor said.

“It’s rare for me to work on a character where I don’t already know the storyline... So, I’m having the most amazing time in a new process. [I’ve been acting] a long time — it’s so nice to have a new way to look at creating a role, originating a role.”

Chancellor John Healey has reportedly told Cabinet ministers they must prepare for spending cuts to finance Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s new policy pledges.

The directive follows Mr Healey’s announcement that his first budget, set for 28 October, will be "built on fiscal discipline".

Mr Burnham’s premiership has seen a succession of costly announcements, including cost-of-living measures such as a cut in VAT on energy bills and reduced business rates for pubs.

Further plans involve radical devolution across England and an expansion of technical training in schools.

Ministers have been informed, via a joint letter from the Chancellor and the Prime Minister, that no new money is available for these initiatives.

“We’ve written to the Cabinet to say that if we’re serious about new priorities as a second-stage Labour Government we have to be serious about — and they have to be serious about — reprioritisation of their plans, their budgets,” Mr Healey told The Times.

open image in gallery Healey will face significant challenges as he finds more money for Burnham’s devolution priorities ( PA )

“They need to pay for the new things they want to do this year and next year within the budgets they’ve already got.”

In the letter, he wrote that departments need to be “disciplined on spending, looking at the tough choices and being ready to shift funding away from unproductive or legacy programmes that no longer reflect this administration’s priorities”.

Mr Healey will face significant challenges as he finds more money for Mr Burnham’s devolution priorities and increased defence spending amid warnings the Iran war will further squeeze the public finances.

He will also have to set out how the Government will fund £5 billion of defence spending announced in May’s Defence Investment Plan (Dip) without details of how it would be paid for.

He will come under pressure to increase that funding further, having resigned as defence secretary ahead of publication of the Dip, arguing it did not provide enough money for the armed forces.

He would not commit to raising defence spending to 3% of GDP by 2030, but suggested it could form part of next year’s spending review.

“At the spending review, we will set out a clear path to meeting our 3.5% Nato commitment in 2035 and we will set a target date on that path for 3%,” he told The Times.

Earlier, he said the budget would “meet our fiscal rules” and “give businesses and families some of the stability they need to plan for the future”.

Looking back at Mr Burnham’s first two weeks as Prime Minister, Mr Healey said the new Government was “working fast to restore hope and back Britain’s communities” and had “begun to kickstart growth in every postcode”.

Experts have warned Mr Healey he will need to raise taxes or cut spending elsewhere as pressure on the public finances has left no room for extra borrowing.

The National Institute of Economic and Social Research (Niesr) said on Wednesday the conflict in Iran would mean more persistent inflation and higher interest rates.

open image in gallery Experts have warned Mr Healey he will need to raise taxes or cut spending elsewhere ( PA )

Stephen Millard, Niesr’s deputy director for macroeconomics, suggested Mr Healey should look at the welfare bill or the pensions triple lock as areas for potential cuts.

He also suggested Mr Healey should consider raising income tax, which would break Labour’s 2024 manifesto pledge not to raise that levy, national insurance or VAT.

That pledge, along with the fiscal rules set by former chancellor Rachel Reeves on borrowing, are likely to constrain Mr Healey’s room for manoeuvre.

In a letter to Commons Treasury Committee chairwoman Dame Meg Hillier, the Chancellor stressed his commitment to fiscal discipline.

He said: “Fiscal credibility is the bedrock of economic stability and national security.

“That is why we will abide by the fiscal rules, ensuring we retain a buffer to protect us against uncertainty and the impact of instability in the Middle East.”

In her last budget, Ms Reeves left a £22 billion buffer against her fiscal rules, but persistent inflation due to the Iran war could have eaten away at this.

Shadow chancellor Sir Mel Stride said the announcement of the budget date meant “89 more days of unfunded spending commitments and damaging tax speculation until we get some details”, and “89 more days for Brits to wait before they know how much their taxes are going to go up to fund Burnham’s spending addiction”.

He added: “Only the Conservatives have a plan to cut spending by £50 billion starting with the welfare bill, so we can cut taxes, lower your bills and back business to deliver a stronger economy and a stronger country.”

Georgia Hunter Bell felt “really calm” in winning gold in the 800 metres final at Scotstoun Stadium even though the race did not go to plan.

The Olympic bronze medallist from Paris at 1500m, who also won silver at the 2025 World Championships at 800m, demonstrated her class in her first Commonwealth Games.

The 32-year-old English runner led at the bell after dominating the first lap then stepped it up coming down the home straight to leave her challengers behind, finishing in 1:59.51.

open image in gallery Georgia Hunter Bell celebrates her 800m victory at Scotstoun Stadium (Martin Rickett/PA) ( PA Wire )

Kenyan Lilian Odira was second in 2:00.58 with Australia’s Sarah Billings taking bronze in 2:00.61, while Isabelle Boffey of Wales finished fifth.

Hunter Bell said: “I felt really calm. I felt calm. I really feel like I was composed. It didn’t go to plan as in the race.

“I did not think I would do a gun to tape and lead it for the whole thing.

“I wanted to lead with, like, 200 to go. But I found myself at the front and so I thought, I’ll just control it, keep it relaxed, not too fast.

open image in gallery Hunter Bell, centre, celebrates with runner-up Lilian Odira and bronze medallist Sarah Billings (Martin Rickett/PA) ( PA Wire )

“And then when I feel that pressure on me with a move being made, I’ll be ready to go.”

Hunter Bell was pleased to hear the Glasgow crowd cheer her to the finish line.

She said: “It was very emotional (on podium). I think I’ve just felt really supported here.

“The crowd has been really nice to me even though I’m English, which I wasn’t sure if I would get.

“But everyone has been just great and especially that last little bit of the race.

“I thought like my legs were going, but the crowd like really got me there. So yeah, so happy.

“I’ve never done a Commonwealth Games before, so I really wanted to experience it.

“I really wanted the opportunity to win medals.

“I think every athlete is different and I had to pull out of London (Diamond League) a couple of weeks ago because I was sick and you can have a plan of what you want to do, but you have to adapt as the season goes.

“So, yeah, I wanted to be here and I’m very happy that I could be here and that the sickness didn’t linger too long.”

England’s Emily Newnham won silver in the women’s 400m hurdles final, beaten by Sanique Walker of Jamaica.

Jake Minshull of England also took silver in the men’s 400m hurdles final with Nigeria’s Ezekiel Nathaniel taking gold.

A man who sued Kim Kardashian’s associates for defamation, alleging his photograph was mistakenly used in an online post about a death row inmate, has abandoned his appeal. Ivan Cantu had claimed his image was wrongly associated with an inmate of the same name awaiting execution in Texas in early 2024.

Los Angeles Superior Court Judge Michael C. Small ruled in favor of the 45-year-old Kardashian on November 5, dismissing Cantu’s case. This decision followed arguments on her anti-SLAPP motion, heard October 14.

Cantu appealed the ruling on December 30, but his attorney filed court papers on Tuesday with Judge Small, confirming the appeal's abandonment. No reason for this decision was provided.

Cantu’s initial lawsuit, filed in February 2025, alleged defamation, false light invasion of privacy, intentional infliction of emotional distress and negligence. A May 28, 2025, amendment later added a claim for misappropriation of likeness.

A Los Angeles Superior Court judge ruled in favor of the 45-year-old Kardashian on November 5 ( Steven Tee/Getty Images )

In May of this year, Small granted Kardashian $167,475 in attorneys' fees and $1,062 in costs as the prevailing party in the anti-SLAPP motion.

In their opposition to Kardashian's attorneys' fees request, Cantu's lawyers contended that the anti-SLAPP statute was "not intended to so severely punish an innocent victim who suffered injuries due to defendant's admitted error and due to the clear inequity of the financial status of the parties, which would punish Mr. Cantu unfairly due to defendant's wealth, power and ability to easily pay her attorney's outrageously high fees."

The state's anti-SLAPP (Strategic Lawsuit Against Public Participation) law is intended to prevent people from using courts, and potential threats of a lawsuit, to intimidate those who are exercising their First Amendment rights. Cantu's attorneys further stated in their pleadings that if Small was inclined to award attorneys' fees and costs that he cap the total amount at $5,000.

In his November dismissal ruling, the judge said Cantu did not indicate that he sustained damages because of Kardashian's mistake.

Cantu said in a sworn declaration that the error caused him to receive several online messages from strangers who believed he was going to be executed.

"The post caused me to suffer embarrassment, humiliation, anxiety, emotional and mental anguish, headaches, loss of sleep and loss of reputation," Cantu said.

Nearly two-thirds of American children, aged 2-19 years old, have caffeine as a regular part of their daily diet - including half of kids under age 5, a new federal report shows.

Kids consumed an average of 19.4 milligrams of caffeine a day - the majority of a can of original Coca-Cola - between August 2021-2023, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention found.

While it’s a myth that the stimulant can stunt growth, drinking caffeine during childhood can still come with concerning impacts to health.

It can interrupt crucial hours of sleep needed for kids to grow and for their brain to develop, experts say.

“Caffeine-containing foods and beverages can have effects on the body and mind that interfere with every aspect of what children need to thrive,” Columbia University Irving Medical Center pediatrician Dr. David Buchholz said in a prior statement.

open image in gallery This chart from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention shows the percentage of youth between the ages of 2-19 who have caffeine in their diet on any given day from August 2021-2023, broken down by age group, sex, race and Hispanic origin. There is no known safe amount of caffeine for kids age 11 and younger ( CDC )

Interrupting a child’s sleep cycle increases symptoms of anxiety, creates stomach problems and - in some cases - can lead to a dependency on caffeine or even a rare fatal overdose.

An increase in heart rate and adrenaline after chugging caffeine can cause the electrical system of the heart to “misfire,” Dr. Paul Thompson, co-physician-in-chief of the Hartford HealthCare Heart & Vascular Institute, explained in 2017.

Other symptoms include headaches, dehydration, diarrhea and high blood pressure, the medical center noted.

Part of the problem is that kids are smaller than adults and it takes much less caffeine to cause problems. While adults are able to handle around 400 milligrams of caffeine a day, there is no known safe amount of caffeine for anyone age 11 and younger.

Teens should limit their consumption to no more than 100 milligrams - or one cup of coffee. But many energy drinks popular with teens far exceed that amount, the American Academy of Pediatrics says.

“This might be why so many labels carry warnings that the drink is meant for adults only,” the academy wrote.

The academy says kids and teens should not consume energy drinks.

Drinks aren’t the only products to blame, either. Candy and sweet bakery products were in the top five sources of caffeine consumed by youth, the CDC report said.

Products that parents might feel safe to serve for dessert could have more caffeine than they realize, as well as bad sugar that leaves children at risk of developing obesity or diabetes.

“A 3.5-ounce dark chocolate bar might have anywhere from 50-150 milligrams of caffeine. Ice cream, protein bars, chocolate chips, energy bars and even chewing gum can have hidden caffeine,” the academy explained. “Nutrition labels do not have to list caffeine content.”

open image in gallery Many kids eat chocolate and other sweet treats. Caffeine can be lurking inside and candy and sweet bakery products were in the top five sources of caffeine consumed by youth ( Getty Images )

There are several recommended practices to help kids and teens to avoid caffeine. First, remind children where it may be lurking and explain what could happen to them if they have too much.

Second, ensure they are getting enough water. On a typical day - without extreme heat as a factor - younger children aged 1-3 might only need four cups of water, but those aged 4-8 need five cups and older kids need 7-8 cups, the Seattle Children’s Hospital says.

Teenagers need 10 or more cups, according to the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics.

And lastly, there’s no substitute for good sleep. Preschoolers should get 10-13 hours, older kids should get between 9-12 hours and teens should get between 8-10 hours, per the CDC.

“If you suspect your child or teen may be struggling with sleep deprivation, consulting a health care or mental health professional can help you determine a path toward restoring good sleep habits and ensuring a successful future,” the Mayo Clinic advises.

Massachusetts is moving to grant doctors the final authority on late-term abortions, a legislative change intended to prevent women from being turned away from care.

The state Senate adopted the measure on Friday, sending it to Democratic Governor Maura Healey, a known proponent of strengthening abortion rights.

Under current Massachusetts law, abortion is legal for the first 24 weeks of pregnancy. Beyond this, it is permitted only if a physician deems it necessary for the woman's life, physical or mental health, due to a lethal fetal anomaly, or if the fetus is unlikely to survive outside the uterus.

State Representative Christine Barber highlighted how this framework has led to hospitals refusing abortions late in pregnancy, even in cases where a fetus had suffered a stroke and was not expected to live.

open image in gallery The state Senate adopted the measure on Friday, sending it to Democratic Governor Maura Healey, a known proponent of strengthening abortion rights ( Getty Images )

The new legislation seeks to remove this prescriptive list of reasons, instead stipulating that late-term abortions would be permitted solely "based on the professional judgment of the physician."

Opponents say that it would allow abortion until birth — even on healthy fetuses — and that later abortions are more complex and risky for the women.

“While this legislation prioritizes access, it does not prioritize a woman’s safety,” Myrna Maloney Flynn, president of Massachusetts Citizens for Life, said in a video encouraging supporters to tell lawmakers to reject the bill.

Abortion law changes have slowed but not stopped

If Healey signs it, the law would be the latest change to a U.S. abortion landscape that received a shock four years ago after a Supreme Court ruling that overturned Roe v. Wade and allowed states to enforce abortion bans.

Some already had bans on the books as they waited for permission to enforce them, and others adopted bans or restrictions after the ruling. Currently, 13 states are enforcing bans on abortion at all stages of pregnancy, with some exceptions. Another four bar it after about six weeks of pregnancy — which is often before women realize they are pregnant.

Several Democratic-controlled states have moved the other way, adding laws that seek to protect medical providers from prosecution for providing abortion to patients in other states. Massachusetts is among the states that has gone farthest, with a shield law that applies to those who prescribe abortion bills via telehealth to women in states where abortion is banned. Anti-abortion officials in Louisiana and Texas are testing those protections.

Most abortion-related state laws adopted this year have not made for major changes on when or how abortion is allowed.

For instance, a new Colorado law requires colleges that have student health centers to provide abortion pills for students starting in August 2027. Private schools that say it conflicts would their religious beliefs would be exempt.

A new Oklahoma law makes it a felony to buy or sell those pills for the purpose of an unlawful abortion for someone else.

News.title: Battle rages over access to new ‘miracle’ HIV drug
News.content:
For the first time in the four-decade fight against HIV there is a “miracle” drug that can all but eliminate the risk of infection, but in the Latin American countries where it was tested almost no one can get it.

Trials show that Lenacapavir, made by Gilead Sciences, is almost 100 per cent effective in preventing HIV infection. With just two shots a year, those taking it will avoid contracting the virus even when frequently exposed.

The drug, which many believe could bring an end to the global HIV pandemic, costs $14,000 a dose in the United States. Gilead has agreed to licence generic versions of the pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) medication at around $40 a dose in 120 low-and middle-income countries, but almost all of Latin America is excluded.

Brazil, Mexico, Argentina and Peru are among those with serious HIV epidemics that are shut out, despite having run some of the clinical trials that proved the drug works.

Their status as “upper-middle income countries” means they are too rich to qualify for the cut price generic version and yet they remain too poor to pay the US price.

News.title: Senior dating: a guide to finding love later in life
News.content:
Whether you’re a widow, widower or divorcee, the thought of online dating in later life can feel daunting. However, more and more people are turning to the internet to find romance. Roughly 16 per cent of UK adults are using online dating services to meet a partner, according to Statista. Among them, there are lots of singles over 50 using dating sites.

So here’s how to navigate your senior dating online, with expert advice from psychologist and dating coach Dr Pam Spurr, and sex and relationship coach Angela Vossen.

How do I know if I'm ready to date again as a senior?

Coming out of any relationship is hard. If you’re hoping to date after a divorce, bereavement or break up, it can take a long time to feel ready to date again. Dr Spurr advises taking your time.

“Many people feel bruised, even traumatised, after coming out of a long-term relationship or having been bereaved,” she explains. “Your feelings naturally vary from day to day about whether you're ready to get back out to look for love – or even for fun. A crucial factor is if you've come to the point where you have more good days compared to bad days”.

Dr Spurr explains that good days are the days on which you feel more optimistic about life generally, and you find your thoughts turning to meeting someone new. “That's an important sign that you are healing,” she says. “However, if you're still feeling deeply insecure or are riddled with self-doubt about your worthiness, take your time. When you feel worthy, you will find someone worthy of you”.

Feeling heartbroken? Learn how to get over a break up

How to start senior dating online

If you’re new to online dating, it can feel intimidating at first. The secret is taking things step by step so that you do things at your own pace. The first step, however, should be choosing a senior dating site that will help match you with like-minded people. This will narrow your search and ensure your dating experience is more successful.

Step 1: Create an online profile

Once you’ve decided on a dating site or app and signed up, you’ll be asked to write a dating profile. This should reflect who you are along with your passions, values and what you seek in a partner.

Try to be authentic rather than creating a fantasy version of yourself. If you exaggerate your accomplishments, your date will only feel deceived once they get to know you. Likewise, don’t be tempted to use a photo of yourself from 10 years ago.

What are you waiting for? |  Single and looking to find true love? Sign up today for Telegraph Dating and join more than 220,000 like-minded people. Join today

Step 2: Spark meaningful chats with potential dates

Once you have signed up to a senior dating site and created a profile, you will be free to start looking at other people’s profiles and sending messages to anyone that catches your attention. But how can you initiate a conversation after an introduction?

“When messaging people on dating sites, ask open-ended questions to spark meaningful chats,” says Angela. A good example would be, ‘I can see you enjoy travel. What place have you always wanted to visit but haven’t yet?’ or “tell me more about your love of tennis? Did you watch the US Open?” If things go really well and the chat seems to flow naturally, you may decide to organise a phone chat or ask them out on a date. An initial chat over the phone can help gauge how well you get on and how easily the conversation flows. If this goes well, meeting in person may feel less nerve wracking and a little less ‘blind’.

Step 3: Prioritise your safety

“While most people are well intentioned online, it’s important to protect your safety,” advises Ms Vossen. “Keep personal details private (like where you live or your social media profiles) until you’ve met in person and built trust”. You should also arrange first dates in public places, share your plans with a friend, and trust your instincts if something feels off.

If the first date or two doesn’t quite hit the mark, try not to be too disappointed and remember that you can say no to another date. Ms Vossen says: “Be patient – online dating takes time, but with practice, you’ll gain confidence and enjoy the journey”.

Traditional ways to meet senior singles

Of course, couples continue to meet in a manner that predates online dating sites. If you’re keen to join the older dating scene but find the online world overwhelming, there are plenty of ways to meet people in real life.

1. Holidays and group trips

We are often our best selves on holiday, so it’s the ideal place to find a single senior woman or to meet men if the opportunity presents itself. Why not organise a trip on which you meet new people while doing what you love, whether that’s cycling, walking, sightseeing or just travelling around a new part of the world. There are many escorted tours that cater to specific age groups and interests. They also take away the stress of organising a trip yourself.

“An organised holiday or trip can be a great place to meet someone new and there are many organisations offering these for the over 50s,” says Dr Spur. “A word of caution though, you can spend a lot of money and there's no guarantee that you will meet that special person. However, if it's a place you've wanted to travel to then go with the mindset that you're going to have a great trip. If you meet someone, that's an added bonus”.

2. Activities and social groups

Whether you enjoy walking, reading or volunteering, taking up a new hobby or joining a social group is a great way to enhance your social life and increase your chances of meeting a new romantic interest.

“Joining a club or taking up a hobby can be a fantastic way of meeting singles who enjoy the same pastimes,” says Dr Spur. “You're doing an activity you enjoy knowing that there might also be someone there that will catch your eye”.

If you do meet someone that you’re interested in at a social event, Dr Spur advises starting with a simple ‘hello’ and an easy question such as how long they've been doing that particular activity or hobby. “This can open-up a friendly conversation that might lead to flirting down the line,” she says.

Start online dating for seniors today

Whichever way you decide to start looking for love, approach it in a way that you feel comfortable with. Signing up to an online dating service is a great way to meet other seniors. Remember, it’s never too late to begin a new chapter.

News.title: UK economy to flatline, warns Bank of England
News.content:
Britain’s economy is set to almost grind to a halt for the rest of the year, the Bank of England has warned.

Growth will drop to just 0.1pc per quarter, the Bank predicted, slowing sharply after a strong start to 2026.

Higher petrol prices and energy bills, a weak jobs market and rising mortgage costs are all draining confidence and spending power from the economy.

Inflation, which slowed to a 15-month low of 2.6pc in June, is also expected to rise again to 3.2pc later this year, the Bank warned.

Andrew Bailey, the Bank’s Governor, said inflation had “fallen faster than we’d expected” but warned that war in the Middle East would lead to a fresh spike.

He added that growth would “weaken slightly further in the near term as the effects of the conflict weigh further on demand”.

The Bank also predicted that unemployment will rise back above 5pc in the coming months, limiting workers’ ability to ask for higher wages to cope with rising living costs.

It presents a challenging backdrop for Andy Burnham and his Chancellor, John Healey, who have pledged to help voters struggling with the cost of living.

The forecasts came as policymakers led by Mr Bailey held interest rates at 3.75pc.

Although three members of the nine-strong Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) voted for higher rates, up from two at the previous meeting, the Governor dismissed suggestions the Bank is moving towards higher interest rates.

The public should “not… [think] the Bank of England is edging towards a hike,” Mr Bailey said.

“Frankly there is nothing I have said, or any of us have said, along those lines. We took a decision today to leave the Bank Rate unchanged and that is the relevant conclusion.”

Clare Lombardelli, a Deputy Governor, said voting to keep rates at 3.75pc “was not a close judgement”, calling the decision “pretty clear” given slowing inflation in the domestic economy.

Officials are monitoring the economy for any signs that increases in oil, gas and petrol prices caused by the war in Iran are creeping into higher costs and wages in the wider economy.

Mr Bailey said: “The possibility of repeated resumptions of conflict, combined with lower than usual European gas stock levels and a fall in global refining output, mean that risks to energy prices lie to the upside.”

He added: “Reassuringly, there are few signs so far that second-round effects are generating more broad-based inflationary pressures.”

Companies are struggling to pass higher costs on to their customers because of the economy’s weakness, he added.

Workers are typically securing only modest pay rises as the weak jobs market leaves them in a poor position to push for bigger salaries.

Mr Bailey stressed there are still major risks to the outlook given the war and promised to “monitor the situation carefully” and was “ready to adjust our stance”.

“It is our job to ensure that inflation gets back to the 2pc target and stays there, and that is what we will do,” he said.

Borrowing costs dropped in financial markets after the decision.

The Government’s two-year borrowing cost fell from 4.44pc to 4.34pc, the sharpest fall in a month.

The FTSE 250 index of mid-sized UK companies rose 0.8pc to a record high of 24,184.10.

Traders still believe the Bank will raise interest rates twice within a year.

However, Paul Dales, chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said rate rises “remain more a threat than a reality”.

He said there was evidence of disinflation in the economy and interest rates could be “cut to 3pc in 2027”, adding: “That’s very different to market pricing for rates to be close to 4.5pc in 2027.”

News.title: Arsonists torch more Ebola clinics as misinformation spirals in DRC
News.content:
Two more Ebola treatment facilities have reportedly been burned down in recent days as health officials struggle to overcome violent public mistrust of medical teams.

At least a dozen facilities have now been attacked since Congo declared its Ebola outbreak amid fear, misinformation and suspicion of outside authorities.

The outbreak is the fastest growing on record and officials said the virus had now killed more than 1,500 people.

The official death toll from the outbreak centred on the north eastern Ituri province of Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has risen by 500 in only a week.

Sources told the Telegraph the large jump in deaths was largely caused by a “data harmonisation exercise” between different regions, and the new deaths may not have all happened in the past week.

However, the daily confirmed toll has also continued to climb sharply with the latest government update reporting 50 people dying in the previous 24 hours.

Airfinity, a health analytics firm, said the outbreak “continues to outpace detection and the response” and there is a high chance of it spreading further inside DRC.

News.title: Race for vaccine against new Ebola strain gets $8.5m boost
News.content:
The “most promising” vaccine to tackle the Ebola strain behind an explosive outbreak in the Congo has been given an $8.5 million boost, as researchers race to develop an effective shot.

So far at least 3,360 people have been infected and 1,487 people have died in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), in an epidemic triggered by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola.

But unlike past outbreaks of the more common Zaire strain, there are currently no approved vaccines to tackle Bundibugyo.

On Thursday, the Coalition of Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (Cepi) revealed up to $8.5 million of funding for the only single-dose inoculation, which was described as the “most promising vaccine candidate” by the World Health Organization (WHO) in an analysis in May.

It is being developed by researchers at Hilleman Laboratories – a unique partnership between the pharmaceutical giant Merck and the British philanthropic powerhouse Wellcome, which is headquartered in Singapore.

The vaccine candidate is a Bundibugyo version of the Ervebo shot, which was created by Merck (MSD in Europe) and has already been approved for Ebola Zaire.

It uses a rVSV platform, where a modified version of VSV virus is used to train the immune system to react to target pathogens – in this instance, the Bundibugyo species replaces Zaire.

News.title: AMR chatbot could prevent drug-resistant infections in African hospitals
News.content:
A phone-based chatbot advising medics how to prescribe antibiotics has helped raise the quality of care in African hospitals and should stop bugs developing dangerous resistance, developers say.

Staff at four hospitals across Zambia and Kenya have been using two digital tools in a pilot project to try to address one of the world’s biggest health threats.

Anti-microbial resistance (AMR) is caused by germs evolving so that medicines such as antibiotics designed to kill them no longer work.

The menace is linked to nearly five million deaths each year and makes it increasingly difficult to treat infections. The annual death toll could nearly double in the next 25 years, according to some forecasts.

The rise in AMR is being significantly driven by the misuse and overuse of antimicrobials in human medicine and in agriculture.

Using antibiotics when they are not necessary, using the wrong ones, or getting the dosage wrong, all add to the chances that bugs will develop resistance.

With a shortage of new drugs in the development pipeline, one push to defeat AMR has been to get medics to stick to existing prescription, dosage and treatment advice.

The Antibiotic Stewardship Programme through Innovation, Research, and Education (ASPIRE) is trying to give them guidance using technology they already have in their pockets.

News.title: Tottenham new boys score in shoot-out win over Sydney FC
News.content:
Tonali was brought on as a half-time substitute, before Robertson took the captain’s armband from Archie Gray after he was introduced in the 65th minute.

The former Liverpool left-back delivered three dangerous crosses which went unconverted, something of a theme for a Spurs team who failed to make the most of long spells of dominance.

James Maddison and Mateus Fernandes were not in the match-day squad, while Pedro Porro, Marcos Senesi, Cristian Romero, Micky van de Ven and Jean Paul van Hecke have yet to join the group after the World Cup.

There was another impressive showing from 17-year-old prospect Luca Williams-Barnett, who is pushing for first-team opportunities this upcoming season.

Penalties followed the final whistle, with Spurs scoring all four of their spot kicks. Goalkeeper Martin Dubravka, signed on a free transfer this summer, saved one and Sydney FC’s Josh Lacey hit the post to give Spurs the spoils 4-2.

News.title: Recovery aids and building muscle: Welsh weightlifter Laura Hughes answers your questions
News.content:
Laura Hughes first discovered weightlifting while training at her local Crossfit gym, making the transition from amateur gym-goer to competitive lifting.

Now a member of the Welsh national weightlifting squad, the 33-year-old holds the Welsh record for both the snatch and the clean and jerk (the two official competitive lifts in weightlifting) and is currently third overall in the women’s Welsh rankings. Hughes won bronze at this year’s Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, following on from her third place at the 2018 Games in Australia.

We caught up with her for our Readers Ask series, where industry specialists answer questions from our Telegraph Recommended Reader Panel.

Who inspired you to get into weightlifting?

Olamilekan, South East

Originally, it was lots of different people, particularly general gym goers who were doing weightlifting at my gym. As I’ve grown as an athlete and become more competitive, I’ve had other inspirations.

Most notably, coming into [the Commonwealth Games], it has to be Gareth [Evans], our coach. Looking back at his performance in 2018 when he won his gold medal is so inspiring. [English lifter] Emily Godley was another competitor in 2018. She won the gold medal in my category and I just remember thinking that she was on fire that day.

What are the best exercises for you to build muscle mass?

Norman, Wales

We spend a lot of time doing our main lifts, so snatches, clean and jerks, but we also do lots of pulls and squats. I spend a lot of time doing accessory work to make sure that my body stays healthy, especially being an older athlete. I’ve put on quite a lot of muscle in this last block just from going heavier and pushing my limits with my main lifts.

What advice would you give to people who want to improve their strength?

David, North West

The most important thing is consistency. As long as you’re doing something, do it regularly, even if it’s twice a week. Don’t be afraid of picking up some dumbbells. If you’ve got somebody that can teach you how to lift weights properly, that’s going to be the best option. Do it safely, do it consistently, and don’t be afraid to try new strength exercises.

Sports.title: ‘If I lose my job, so be it’ – Fifa COO accuses Gianni Infantino of ‘deceiving’ governing body in blistering statement
Sports.content:
FIFA chief operating officer Kevin Lamour has blasted president Gianni Infantino’s shameless plot to flog stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

Infantino, 56, wants to sell off shares related to the organisation’s commercial and event operations, with the estimation being it could raise £7.52billion.



The Swiss official’s controversial idea was met with fury by Uefa, who unanimously agreed to boycott all Fifa-related competitions until he rescinds his unpopular plan.

Concacaf swiftly followed by rejecting the outlandish World Cup plans before AFC also slammed the initiative and Infantino’s senior advisor Carlos Cordeiro resigned in protest.



According to The Times, the Fifa president is now fighting for his future and some believe his days are numbered.

And Lamour became the latest to slam Infantino’s idea insisting Fifa were never on board with it.

The COO is adamant this whole initiative was down to Infantino alone and he is personally so against it he is willing to step down.

Lamour said: “To put it very clearly and directly: the project that has sparked so much controversy and debate is not a Fifa project. It is even less a project of Fifa’s administration. It is the project of one person.

“The Fifa vice-presidents, the members of the Fifa Council, the confederations, the federations, the players, the leagues, the clubs, and the fans were not the only ones who were ignored.

“Fifa’s own administration was also deceived. This lie by omission over many months and this unilateral exercise of power are not trivial.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“They are indicative of a lack of trust, a lack of transparency, a lack of discernment, a lack of good governance. And a serious lack of respect.

“Not only must this project not go ahead — for obvious reasons that need not even be listed here — but the time has now come for football political leaders to ask themselves the right questions and make the right decisions.

“Regarding this project and what comes next. Everyone must take responsibility. Because it is becoming increasingly difficult for Fifa’s administration to work under these conditions and fulfil its mission.

“My feeling is that we all want to be proud to work for Fifa, and today, unfortunately, it seems that is no longer the case for many of us. That saddens me.



“My colleagues — some of whom have dedicated their lives to football — deserve better than contempt and intimidation.

“The ball is now in the court of those who have the power to change things. I know I have a duty of loyalty to my employer.

“But I also, and above all, have a duty of loyalty to certain values and to the upbringing I have received, and a duty to support my colleagues.

“And if that means I lose my job, then so be it. I will understand and respect that decision. At least I’ll sleep well tonight.”

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham also criticised Infantino and called for his resignation.



Fifa, though, issued a statement of their own insisting the plans in question wouldn’t harm football’s reputation.

It read: “Nobody is selling football. This is not something Fifa would ever entertain.

“Our planned consultation process was disrupted by incorrect media reports.

“We will proceed with this consultation process to ensure that each MA [member association] has the ability to express its vote based on facts.”

Sports.title: From City’s superhero goalie kit to Action Man Stoke & Newcastle’s barcode, the wacky new strips that need a VAR check
Sports.content:
WITH the footie season kicking off this month, many of the top sides’ new football shirts have been released.

While some score highly, other wackier designs might need a VAR check . . . especially with fans facing a bill of up to £90 to buy their official replica shirt.



From Elvis-inspired tops to cult film nods and animated associations, our fashion team Abby McHale and Emily Regan offer their pick of the latest strips – from the stylish to those that maybe should have been sent for an early bath.

Newcastle United home

NEWCASTLE are no stranger to a ­winning formula with their kit, sticking with the club’s famous black and white stripes since 1894.



This season however The Magpies have made a subtle tweak, with a barcode-like design that bears a striking resemblance to something you might find at the supermarket checkout.

We’re not sure this shirt will register with the fans, though rivals have already been known to refer to them as the Barcodes.

Man City keeper

THIS is the new goalies’ shirt for City, and it looks like they want their keepers to have superpowers.

The orangey red geometric print resembles Spider-Man’s famous suit, with his super–human speed and agility – exactly what you need between the sticks in a tricky moment.



Ipswich Town away

THE Ipswich 26/27 away shirt feels like a blast from the past.

The Tractor Boys have leaned into a nostalgic beige with horizontal retro lines.

Sometimes less is more, but in this case it feels like less is . . . well, less.

And with Ed Sheeran as a sleeve ­sponsor, it looks like they’ve hit the rewind button.



Stoke City away

WHILE the sentiment behind long-term Championship side Stoke’s away kit is appreciated (it pays homage to the Spitfire and is said to embody innovation, resilience and a proud connection to British history), we just can’t help but think with its camouflage design the players could have trouble finding each other on the pitch.

The Potters’ fans who part with their hard-earned cash to buy this top may think they’re channelling Action Man but, to be honest, it’s giving out more of a fancy dress vibe.

Brentford away

ALTHOUGH the words suave and sophisticated are not often levelled at the West Londoners, their away kit this season attempts just that.



Created in collaboration with Brentford shareholder Sir Matthew Vaughn – the director of the Kingsman films – the pinstripe shirt look is meant to be a homage to the craftsmanship and ­heritage of Savile Row.

Hopefully this will help The Bees to sew up another ­season in the top flight as they attempt to do the business on the pitch.

Bournemouth home

DESPITE Bournemouth sticking with their trademark red and black stripes for the home shirt, the stripes are thicker than usual.

This tweaked design gives an uncanny resemblance to Dennis The Menace’s famous jumper.



While the team get ready to sink their Gnashers into the new season, it is going to be hard to shake the Beano comparison.

Sunderland away

THIS season, the Black Cats are taking inspiration from their long-time association with Elvis Presley.

Since the Seventies, fans have belted out his hit Can’t Help ­Falling In Love as their match anthem.

And now the club have collaborated with the Elvis Presley estate.



The team’s new matchday shirt for fans ­honours The King thanks to a black and pink colour combo and ­diamond design, with Can’t Help Falling In Love stitched on the back.

It’s a fitting tribute to Elvis, but looks more suitable for Graceland than the Stadium Of Light.

Hull City home

AFTER being promoted from the Championship, Hull City are entering the big league after nine years away – and they look ready to roar.

There really is no getting away from the orange and black colour palette associated with the club – and the tiger on their crest.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Sports.title: Georgina Rodriguez puts on eye-popping display in black bikini amid Cristiano Ronaldo wedding rumours
Sports.content:
GEORGINA RODRIGUEZ enjoyed herself by the sea amid Cristiano Ronaldo wedding rumours.

The stunning model, 32, has been with the former Manchester United superstar for a decade.



The happy couple finally got engaged last year, Georgina confirming the news by posting a picture of her huge engagement ring to Instagram.

In her most recent Insta post, the Argentine uploaded several snaps of herself by the sea.



One picture featured Georgina wearing a black bikini and baseball cap aboard a plush boat.

While in another she relaxed on the beach.

The second picture saw her pose alongside Ronaldo and son Cristiano Jr.

And she even posted a clip of Cristiano Jr on a jet ski.

Ronaldo, 41, was spotted wearing a huge diamond on his ring finger, reminiscent of the one he gave Georgina to mark their engagement.

This sparked rumours of a wedding this weekend, with some local press even claiming that it will take place at the Quinta da Regaleira estate in Sintra, Portugal.



The venue appears to be open to the public this weekend, however, casting major doubt over the claims.

Georgina seems to be relaxed over the situation, captioning her latest Insta post: “Shinrin-yoku”.

This means “Forest bathing” in Japanese and is a form of therapeutic relaxation.



Ronaldo previously claimed that he planned to marry Georgina after the World Cup, even telling Piers Morgan: “I hope to arrive at my wedding with the champion’s trophy.”

He added: “I’m going to marry her because I believe it’s the right time.

“Not just because she’s the mother of my children — but because she’s the person I love most.”

Sports.title: Premier League star Kaoru Mitoma, 29, dodges prison sentence after car crash that put woman in hospital
Sports.content:
PREMIER LEAGUE star Kaoru Mitoma has dodged a prison sentence and fine in Japan – despite the Brighton winger putting a woman in hospital after a car accident.

Tokyo police questioned Mitoma following a collision in the capital city on July 8.



A female cyclist was rushed to hospital after the footballer reportedly ran a red light and knocked her off her bike at a junction.

The woman, 48, was treated for hand injuries and signed off work for two weeks.



Tokyo public prosecutors studied the case, and considered charging Mitoma with causing injury through dangerous driving.

But they announced on Friday morning that the 31-cap Japan international will escape prosecution because both parties ignored traffic signals.

They said they had reached their verdict “considering that both parties were running a red light, and the content of other related evidence.”

Japanese media quoted updated traffic rules and described the junction’s complex layout as reasons for the prosecutors’ decision.

Mitoma has been recovering from a hamstring injury suffered at the end of last season, which caused him to miss Japan’s World Cup campaign.

Brighton signed him from home-country club Kawasaki Frontale in 2021.



The winger has since made 135 Seagulls appearances, scoring 27 goals.

His advisors declared after the incident: “We sincerely apologise for the great inconvenience and concern caused to the injured party, and all involved due to the accident.

“Mitoma himself takes this accident very seriously, and is responding with condolences and apologies to those affected.

“The victims have been treated by medical institutions and diagnosed with bruises, but Mitoma himself is not injured.

“We take this matter seriously, fully cooperate with the investigation by related agencies, and strive to thoroughly promote safe driving awareness and strengthen compliance education to prevent recurrence.



“Once again, we deeply apologise to those affected, their families, and all involved.”

Sports.title: ‘Enjoyed being our player’ – Bruno Guimaraes breaks silence on Eddie Howe Newcastle exit and drops Arsenal transfer hint
Sports.content:
NEWCASTLE star Bruno Guimaraes issued a touching farewell to departing manager Eddie Howe – and suggested he will soon follow him out the door.

Howe, 48, stepped down from his role after five successful years that saw him leading the Magpies to Champions League qualification and the Carabao Cup – their first honour in 70 years.



The Amersham tactician informed club chiefs he wants to take a break from coaching amid a rough summer that has seen key players Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali going to Barcelona and Tottenham respectively.

Reports suggest the ex-Bournemouth boss knew Bruno, 28, would follow them by joining Arsenal and that was the “final straw”.



The midfielder does indeed appear to be closing in on a move to the Gunners as he was not part of the Newcastle squad that flew out to Spain for their pre-season tour.

The North Londoners are set to pay north of £70million for the Brazil international and personal terms will not be an issue.



So much so that Bruno is waiting for the Premier League clubs to fully agree on a fee so he can undergo a medical with Arsenal.

But as the Prem champions and the Toon iron out terms, the Brazilian took to Instagram to pay tribute to Howe.

The ex-Lyon star initially shared a story of the club’s farewell video for the beloved gaffer and added a short statement.

It read: “King of this club! Thanks for everything you’ve done for us.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“I loved enjoying our time together. Thanks for [making] me a better player and person.”

Bruno then added a final sentence that hinted he may also be on his way out of Tyneside as he hinted he will no longer be “our player”.

He added: “No words I can say will really say how much I enjoyed being our player. Wish all the very best in your future, gaffer.”

Bruno was not done there as he also shared a photo of him and Howe together with a longer and deeper tribute.



The Arsenal target insisted he will never forget the manager’s impact in his career and the belief he showed the last four years as he was the one that brought him in and even named him captain.

Bruno added: “Ed, how could I ever put into words how grateful I am to you?

“First of all, I want to thank you for bringing me to this club. Thank you for everything you’ve done for me, for helping me grow not only as a player, but more importantly as a person.

“You gave me the honour of being captain – of being your captain. That is something I will never forget and will carry with me for the rest of my life.

“Sharing the day-to-day with you and having you as my manager has been a privilege.



“I’m truly grateful for every opportunity, for the trust you placed in me, and for every moment we shared together.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Without a doubt, you are one of the best managers I’ve ever had. Please know that my gratitude will always remain, and that you will always have a friend in me.

“Thank you for everything, I wish you and your family nothing but happiness, success and all the very best.”

Sports.title: Unseen World Cup footage shows Argentine Premier League star keeping distance from Falklands flag as Argentina fans fume
Sports.content:
EMI MARTINEZ has been criticised by some fans in Argentina after footage emerged of the goalkeeper standing apart from team-mates and their controversial Falklands flag.

Argentine Premier League stars Cristian Romero and Lisandro Martinez, as well as ex-Tottenham flop Giovani Lo Celso, unfurled a flag with the message “Las Malvinas son Argentinas” – meaning “The Falklands are Argentine” – after beating England in the World Cup semi-finals.

The gesture provoked fury in England, given the 1982 conflict over the islands that cost hundreds of lives, and that inhabitants have voted overwhelmingly to remain British.



Hothead midfielder Leandro Paredes even doubled down on the controversial celebration after the game by claiming that the Falklands “will always be Argentine”.



In new footage that has emerged of the celebrations, Aston Villa‘s Argentine goalkeeper Martinez can be seen standing apart from the flag waving.

There is no suggestion as to whether this was because he did, or did not, agree with its message.

But some Argentine fans have decided to criticise him nonetheless.

One called him a “disgrace” while another called the supposed gesture “shameful”.

Others used X-rated slurs.

After the match, Martinez praised his team-mates for “playing with a knife between their teeth” and added that England stars “didn’t feel the same way”.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS



When asked if the Falklands conflict had played its part in their motivation, Martinez was not convinced.

He is quoted as saying, in his native Spanish, “I don’t think it’s because of that. It’s in the past. I wasn’t even born.”

Earlier this week, Fifa opened a disciplinary investigation against Argentina for the flag, as well as for their players’ reactions to losing the final to Spain.

Fifa rules ban players from “using a sports event for ­demonstrations of a non-sporting nature”.

In 2014, Argentina were hit with a £20,000 fine for holding up a banner with a similar Falklands message before a match against Slovenia.

Sports.title: Liverpool cult hero, 22, behind famous Alexander-Arnold moment leaves club after eleven years
Sports.content:
LIVERPOOL cult hero Oakley Cannonier – famous for setting up Trent Alexander-Arnold’s legendary assist against Barcelona – has left the club after 11 years.

Cannonier, 22, joined the Reds’ academy in 2015 at the age of 11 following a four-year stint within Leeds’ youth ranks.



The striker competed for the Under-15s all the way up to the Under-21s where he scored five goals in 44 appearances across all youth teams.

But the ex-England youth international’s biggest moment came when he was 14 in 2019 at Anfield where the Merseysiders took on Barcelona in a crunch Champions League semi-final.



Cannonier obviously didn’t play but was still present at the ground as he undertook ball boy duties.

And the academy graduate’s presence proved to be crucial as he had the hindsight to quickly throw the ball at Alexander-Arnold, 27, who in turn immediately crossed a corner-kick for Divock Origi to make it 4-0.

That sealed Liverpool’s incredible comeback – after losing 3-0 in the first leg at the Nou Camp – which in turn paved the way for their sixth European trophy.

After a promising academy career, it looked like the centre-forward would go on to have some more big moments at Anfield.

But a raft of injuries got in the way and the forward was released by the Premier League club this summer before he could ever play for the first team.

Thus, Cannonier signed with Singaporean outfit Hougang United during the summer transfer window.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The forward, though, issued a touching farewell message to Liverpool fans on Instagram where he added a series of photos of his time at the club since he was a kid.

A photo of him celebrating his beloved team’s Champions League comeback against Barcelona was also included.

Cannonier issued the following statement: I would like to say a huge thank you to Liverpool FC for the last 10 years.

“To all the players and SOME of the staff I’ve had the privilege of working with.

“The memories, experiences and friendships I’ve made will stay with me forever.



“This club has played a huge part in my journey, both as a player and as a person, and I’ll always be grateful for that.

“Even though I never got to make my debut at Anfield at least I’m in a little bit of history of this amazing club! YNWA!”

Sports.title: Germany legend Thomas Muller finds love with girlfriend 10 years his junior weeks after quietly splitting from wife
Sports.content:
THOMAS MULLER has a new girlfriend weeks after confirming his split with ex-wife Lisa, according to reports.

Last month it emerged that the former Bayern Munich star, 36, had divorced Lisa following nearly 17 years of his marriage.



The family’s lawyer Christian Schertz said at the time: “The couple separated amicably some time ago. No other statements will be made.”

According to Bild, Muller has found love again, this time with a French woman 10 years his junior.



They report that the German has begun dating Eve Rose Bitbol, 26.

The new couple are said to have recently been together in New Jersey, where Muller worked as a pundit for coverage of the World Cup final on German telly.

Thomas and Eve are also claimed to have been together in Charlotte this week, where the forward took part in the MLS All-Star Game.

Eve attended European business school ESSEC, which is based to the north-west of Paris.

She is now said to work in finance.

Muller uprooted his life last year when he moved to Vancouver Whitecaps following 25 years at Bayern Munich.



At the time it was noted that his wife Lisa had not accompanied him to Canada, with the pair not seen together at a public event since 2024.

Despite this, their split is said to have been on good terms.

Muller has made 32 appearances for the Whitecaps thus far; scoring 14 goals and laying on seven assists.



He helped the MLS All-Stars to a 4-3 victory over a Liga MX side this week, a match in which ex-Tottenham star Son Heung-min netted twice.

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal 'agree terms' with Vinicius Jr, Man Utd Rashford call, Guimaraes latest
Sports.content:
Chelsea and FA drop Mykhailo Mudryk statement

Mykhailo Mudryk will now be available to play for Chelsea. A statement from the FA confirmed the news, saying: "The FA can confirm that the anti-doping disciplinary proceedings against Mykhailo Mudryk were resolved with the agreement of the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) on 30 July 2026.

"In the context of that agreement, Mr Mudryk has accepted his commission of Anti-Doping Rule Violations (ADRVs) and accepted a period of ineligibility. On 22 October 2024, Mr Mudryk was subject to an out-of-competition doping control, which revealed the presence of a low concentration of meldonium, a prohibited substance.

"The FA notified Mr Mudryk of that finding on 4 December 2024 and imposed a provisional suspension. On 23 May 2025, The FA charged Mr Mudryk with ADRVs in breach of Regulations 3 and 4 of its 2024 Anti-Doping Regulations.

"On 7 to 9 January 2026, a hearing took place before an independent Regulatory Commission. The Regulatory Commission found that Mr Mudryk had committed the charged ADRVs and imposed a four-year period of ineligibility. Subsequently, Mr Mudryk filed an appeal with the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

"Since then, changes have been made to WADA Technical Document (TD2027MRL) which, while not retroactive, mean that if Mr Mudryk's sample was collected today, the concentration of meldonium in the sample would not have been reported and no ADRVs would have resulted.

"Further to that development and to other circumstances of the case, The FA and Mr Mudryk have now - with the agreement of WADA - resolved the appeal proceedings in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the World Anti-Doping Code and Regulation 90 of the 2024 Anti-Doping Regulations.

"As a part of the agreement, Mr Mudryk accepted that he had committed the Anti-Doping Rule Violations charged and acceded to a period of ineligibility equal to the time served at the date of the agreement. Mr Mudryk is no longer ineligible and may return to competition with immediate effect."

Chelsea also uploaded their own statement which said: "Chelsea FC acknowledges today's announcement by The Football Association confirming the resolution of the anti-doping proceedings involving Mykhailo Mudryk.

"From the outset, this has been an extremely difficult period for Misha, both professionally and personally, and we are pleased that the matter has now reached a conclusion which allows him to return to football with immediate effect.

"We have always supported Misha throughout this process while fully respecting the integrity of the anti-doping system and the legal process. We welcome the acknowledgement that advances in the applicable scientific reporting standards for more reliable testing mean that, had Misha's sample been analysed under today's technical requirements, it would not have been reported as a positive test and no anti-doping rule violation would have resulted.

"That is an important part of the context surrounding the agreed resolution and allows everyone involved to move forward. "Misha has consistently maintained that he never knowingly or intentionally used a prohibited substance and did not know how traces of the substance entered his system. Throughout this process he has conducted himself professionally and with resilience during what has undoubtedly been one of the most challenging periods of his career.

"We know how much this opportunity to return means to him. Our focus now is on supporting Misha’s reintegration into the squad and helping him resume his career. Chelsea FC remains fully committed to the highest standards of sporting integrity and compliance with all anti-doping regulations. Everyone at the Club now looks forward to helping Misha return to full fitness, back into the squad and back onto the pitch."

Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes has paid an emotional tribute to Eddie Howe after his departure from St James' Park was confirmed

Arsenal transfer target Bruno Guimaraes has paid tribute to Eddie Howe, hailing him as the "King of the club" in a heartfelt message to the departing Newcastle United head coach following confirmation of his exit. The club confirmed Howe's departure earlier today after five years at the helm.

It's another bitter blow for the Magpies during yet another summer of upheaval. Supporters had hoped for a calmer summer interlude than last year, with Alexander Isak's transfer saga dominating the headlines and causing unrest at St. James' Park.

‌



A 4-1 defeat to Bristol City in pre-season was the final act under Howe's tenure, a game in which Guimaraes missed as a result of an extended holiday. The 28-year-old has now taken to social media to share a heartfelt tribute to Howe, which read: "King of this club!

Certain reports suggest Howe's exit was partly down to a feeling that Guimaraes would be sold to the Gunners, having already seen Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali leave the club.

Speaking about Guimaraes following the Bristol City defeat, Howe said: "What will be, will be. We can't control the forces that are at play here, we've just got to make sure that when Bruno comes back, we look after him and he trains well, which I'm sure he will do. And he makes a difference as he always has done.

His training performances and his game performances have been outstanding, every time he's worn the shirt, he's played with the fans by his side. I'd love to see that continue."

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford has chance to 'hurt' Man Utd as two transfer moves proposed
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford has chance to 'hurt' Man Utd as two transfer moves proposed

Marcus Rashford is a Manchester United player on paper, but he has been widely expected to leave the Reds in the transfer window

View 3 Images Marcus Rashford is still facing an uncertain summer (Image: Icon Sportswire, Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

Manchester United have been warned not to sell Marcus Rashford to a Premier League rival. Rene Meulensteen, who was Sir Alex Ferguson's assistant manager at Old Trafford. He believes selling Rashford to the likes of Tottenham Hotspur could hurt the club.

‌



Spurs were recently linked with a £30million move for the England international, whose future at the club is uncertain. Barcelona chose not to sign him permanently, and no club has yet come forward with a meaningful offer for the Reds.

‌



Michael Carrick re-integrating him back into the squad is not impossible, but it's widely been believed both parties feel a clean break is best for everyone. If this is the case, Meulenseteen warned United not to sell to a Premier League rival.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Speaking to Andy's Bet Club, Meulensteen, when questioned whether the scenario might mirror United's choice to sell Scott McTominay, who has since flourished for Napoli, responded: "Would selling Marcus Rashford be a repeat of selling Scott McTominay?

"I don't think people see Scott McTominay the same way. He moved because the club wanted to sell, and he has done brilliantly since. People might wonder if United sold him too early.

‌



"But selling Marcus Rashford to a direct competitor like Arsenal or Chelsea could really hurt you. He is still a player who can make a difference. Ideally, if United sell him, they should sell him abroad."

View 3 Images Barcelona chose not to sign Rashford permanently (Image: Aitor Alcalde Colomer, Getty Images)

Meulensteen also suggested Saudi Arabia could be a potential destination or maybe even the MLS, saying: "Saudi Arabia could be an option for Rashford depending on what he wants," before adding: "Perhaps one of the other big clubs will sign him so he can keep playing in the Champions League. Or he might make a move to Saudi or maybe the MLS, who knows?"

‌



Meulensteen also urged Carrick to open up a dialogue with Rashford to gauge his state of mind and establish how he might contribute to the club. He said: "Michael Carrick is the type of person who recognises Marcus's qualities.

"They need an open conversation so Marcus understands what is required. Michael Carrick won't want to bring someone back if it creates another problem. If the clarity is there, he would be happy to bring him back into the fold.

View 3 Images Michael Carrick still has many options this summer (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



"However, with the other players available, there wouldn't be a guaranteed start every week. The fact that it is taking so long to find clarity suggests there is still something brewing in the background. If all parties were happy for him to come back, they would likely have made that clear very quickly."

When it comes to attacking options, United's primary weapons are Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo, Benjamin Sesko and Amad Diallo, with Bruno Fernandes and Mason Mount frequently operating in the pocket just behind the striker.

Patrick Dorgu was also reinvented as a left-winger under Carrick, chipping in with several crucial goals before an injury derailed his progress last season. United still have further pre-season friendlies remaining on the schedule.
