Sports.content:
'"King of Soccer" Gianni Infantino's plan to sell the soul of football could be final nail in FIFA coffin'

"Gianni Infantino is facing increasing pressure over his handling of the US tournament. FIFA claimed in its latest statement that its plan to sell off a stake in the World Cup 'was disrupted by incorrect media reports'"

Burnham Condemns FIFA Over Secretive US Private Equity World Cup Deal

The latest row over the sale of the World Cup may be the final nail in the coffin for the 'King of Soccer' Gianni Infantino.

‌



The FIFA President is facing increasing pressure over his handling of the US tournament. FIFA claimed in its latest statement that its plan to sell off a stake in the World Cup "was disrupted by incorrect media reports".

‌



But that cut no ice with the English FA, European nations and the Asian Football Confederation. It is yet another controversy on a long list for the Swiss born football chief.

‌



Ironically, he was hailed as the organisation's saviour when he was appointed 10 years ago.

View 4 Images The FIFA President is facing increasing pressure over his handling of the US tournament and his relationship with President Donald Trump (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

Gianni Infantino gets fresh reality check as World Cup boycott grows amid calls for change READ MORE :

Infantino's unlikely route to sporting power began in the small Swiss town of Brig, an Alpine transport hub for nearby ski resorts. As a ginger, freckle-faced youngster, he became president of his local amateur club, FC Brig-Glis, on the mandate that his mother would wash the team's kits. It was the shape of things to come. He is a pragmatist who 'likes to get things done,' according to football insiders.

‌



And that means getting alongside everyone from President Putin - he collected a Russian Order of Friendship from him after the 2018 World Cup - to President Trump, who calls Infantino 'The King of Soccer'.

Born in Switzerland to Italian parents, Infantino is fluent in French, German, Italian, Arabic, English, Portuguese and Spanish. He added Lebanese citizenship to his passport collection under special rules for high-profile figures.

View 4 Images The FIFA President Gianni Infantino with President Donald Trump in the Oval Office (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



His wife and the mother of his four children, Lina al-Ashkar, is Lebanese.

His steady rise started at UEFA in 2000, where he worked in the legal department before becoming deputy general secretary in 2007 and then secretary general in 2009.

After Michel Platini was undone by scandal, Infantino, his former right hand man, was thrust forward for the role. He started his tenure with a low profile, flying to one early meeting on EasyJet.

‌



At this summer's World Cup, he crisscrossed countries on a Qatar Airways private jet.

He pledged to rid football of its reputation for greed and corruption, while looking after UEFA's interests. UEFA backed Infantino with £438,000 to support his campaign.

Ten years on, few of his supporters in European football remain.

‌



FIFA stressed: "Nobody is selling football. This is not something we would ever entertain." But the sky-high prices for the US tournament, Infantino's bizarre award of a 'peace prize' to Trump and now the links to Trump's family in the private investment World Cup plan may signal the end of his tenure. The plans to sell stakes in the tournament to private investors for $20m (£15m) are hugely unpopular. Infantino claims it is about “the democratisation of football worldwide”. But the investor group for FFE would be led by Thrive Eternal.

It was founded earlier this year by Joshua Kushner, the brother of US President Donald Trump ’s son-in-law Jared Kushner.

That has already led to accusations from Democrat Congressman Jamie Raskin that FIFA is “going into business” with the Trump family.

‌



View 4 Images The FIFA HQ in Zurich (Image: Getty Images)

Infantino became Fifa president in 2016 when he beat Asian Football Confederation president Sheikh Salman al-Khalifa by 115 votes to 88. He was due to stand for a fourth term in March.

It had been anticipated he would be re-elected unopposed before the World Cup plan which critics claim 'sells the soul of football'.

‌



Associations around the world had already confirmed their intention to support the 56-year-old. But Concacaf members are losing faith in Infantino.

Nasser Al-Khelaifi, President of Champions League winners Paris St-Germain, is already being touted as his successor.

Former Uefa chief executive Lars-Christer Olsson told the BBC that Infantino has overplayed his hand and his position could be in trouble. When asked if Infantino should be removed from his role, Olsson said: "I think that should be a new start for football."

‌



View 4 Images The FIFA President is facing increasing pressure over his handling of the US tournament (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Infantino opened the Qatar World Cup by saying: "Today I have strong feelings. Today I feel Qatari, I feel Arab, I feel African, I feel gay, I feel disabled, I feel a migrant worker." A total of 6,500 migrant workers from India, Pakistan, Nepal, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka had reportedly died in Qatar since it won its World Cup bid. Infantino added: "We have been taught many lessons by Europeans and the Western world. I am European. For what we have been doing for 3,000 years, we should be apologising for the next 3,000 years before giving moral lessons." Fans around the world criticised his speech. Plans to stage the 2030 World Cup across three continents - Africa, Europe and South America - and the 2034 tournament in Saudi Arabia attracted yet more controversy. Norway's football federation abstained from the process and argued the bidding process undermined "Fifa's reforms for good governance" and challenged "trust in Fifa". In May 2024, it was revealed Infantino received a 33% pay rise, - determined by an independent committee - upon his re-election the previous year. It took his base salary from 1.95m Swiss francs (£1.7m) in 2022 to 2.6m Swiss francs (£2.3m). On top of that, he was due an unchanged bonus of 1.65m Swiss francs (£1.5m).

Infantino, who was earning about £1.3m when first elected in 2016, is now close to Blatter's final annual salary. Infantino handed Trump the controversial FIFA Peace Prize. Within a week came the announcement of high ticket prices for the finals. Then he had to apologise after saying it was "really special" no British nationals were arrested during the 2022 World Cup. His relationship with Trump was thrust into the spotlight when the US President asked FIFA to overturn Folarin Balogun's one-match suspension. USA forward Balogun was sent off during the last-32 tie against Bosnia-Herzegovina but was cleared to feature in the next round after an unprecedented intervention from Trump, which drew widespread criticism. Infantino has offered all 211 of FIFA's member associations $40m (£30m) if they back his controversial plans to sell stakes in the organisation's major competitions - including the World Cup. After being re-elected unopposed in 2019 and 2023, he is approaching another election year in 2027.

Article continues below

Infantino will be able to stand again, even though FIFA statutes limit the president to a maximum of three terms.

His future is on a knife edge though Asia and Africa, the two regions that have benefited from the hugely increased finances, hold almost half of the votes.

Sports.title: Piers Morgan makes Gianni Infantino U-turn as he admits 'I was wrong'
Sports.content:
Piers Morgan makes Gianni Infantino U-turn as he admits 'I was wrong'

FIFA President Gianni Infantino has come under serious criticism for his plan to sell a share in the World Cup to private investors and Piers Morgan has issued his thoughts

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino has been at the centre of controversy once again (Image: Getty Images)

Piers Morgan has called for Gianni Infantino to leave in the midst of his World Cup sale scandal. The FIFA President has found himself at the centre of controversy over the past few weeks, having launched an idea that will see a share of the World Cup sold off to foreign investors.

‌



That plot has not gone down well across the globe, with UEFA, CONCACAF and more federations slamming the plan. The organisers of the European game have also threatened to pull their nations out of any future FIFA competitions should they go through with the plan.

‌



Broadcaster Morgan is among those to have spoken out in opposition and claimed that it is now time for Infantino to step aside.

‌



Taking to social media, he wrote: “I thought FIFA boss Gianni Infantino was a force for good in football. I was wrong. The shameful Balogun fiasco was bad enough, but his greedy, tawdry attempt to flog off the World Cup is beyond the pale. He must go.”

Gianni Infantino ally quits as FIFA boss blasted over World Cup plans in angry statement READ MORE :

Morgan is not the only one to have suggested that Morgan needs to leave his role as FIFA president. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham also questioned his suitability for the job after his World Cup plan was unveiled.

He said: “This was an outrageous suggestion. The idea that it could even be brought forward shows that, in my view, [he] is the wrong man to lead the organisation."

‌



Those comments came after Burnham tore into Infantino’s plan to sell a share in the World Cup. Talking to social media, he said: “Let me say this very directly. Football does not belong to investors. It belongs to the people who fill the stands and who stand on the touchline week in, week out, rain or shine.

“The World Cup is not a product. It is the greatest competition in world sport, and it was never anyone's to sell. Dress the deal up however you like. Once you have sold a piece of it, you have sold out. Football belongs to the fans. It always has, and it always will.”

View 2 Images FIFA's plan to sell a share of the World Cup has been widely criticised (Image: Getty Images)

‌



The fallout from FIFA’s proposal has even worsened over the past couple of days, with Infantino’s senior advisor, Carlos Cordeiro, choosing to resign from his position.

A statement read: "As a Senior Advisor to the FIFA President, a former banker, and a lifelong football fan, I cannot stand by while FIFA considers selling a stake in the World Cup. Let me be clear: I had no involvement in this proposal, and I oppose it unequivocally. It is a bad deal for FIFA's Member Associations, a bad deal for football, and a bad deal for the long-term future of the game.

"Football has been central to my life, and after more than 35 years in banking, I understand both the value of this asset and the consequences of giving part of it away. That is why this proposal should be rejected. FIFA already has access to extraordinary financial resources.

‌



"This proposal has become a defining question for FIFA's future. After careful consideration, I can no longer continue in my role as Senior Advisor to the FIFA President. I have therefore resigned with immediate effect. FIFA's responsibility is not to maximise commercial returns at any cost. It is to protect and strengthen football for future generations. When those principles come into conflict, football must come first.

"It has been the privilege of a lifetime to serve FIFA for more than five years and to work alongside dedicated, principled people who care deeply about the game. I hope they, too, will speak up, because decisions of this magnitude should be made in the interests of football, not those who stand to profit from it."

Sports.title: FIFA chief accuses Gianni Infantino of DECEIVING staff over World Cup plot - 'If I lose my job so be it'
Sports.content:
FIFA chief accuses Gianni Infantino of DECEIVING staff over World Cup plot - 'If I lose my job so be it'

The FIFA president, Gianni Infantino, has come under significant fire over plans to sell stakes in FIFA tournaments such as the World Cup to private investors

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino has been accused of 'deceiving' staff with his World Cup sale plot (Image: GSI/Icon Sport via Getty Images)

The chief operating officer of FIFA has accused Gianni Infantino of 'deceiving' staff in relation to the plot to sell World Cup stakes to private investors, adding the proposal 'must not go ahead'.

‌



Infantino unveiled plans to sell off a portion of FIFA's commercial businesses, including tournaments such as the World Cup and the Club World Cup, to private investors. However, his proposal has been met with a ferocious backlash from football's other governing bodies including UEFA, whose nations are ready to boycott future World Cups if the plans go ahead.

‌



One of the 56-year-old's senior advisors, Carlos Cordeiro, has already resigned over the plans. And now another of Infantino's colleagues has torn into the proposal.

‌



Kevin Lamour, who has been FIFA's COO since 2024, says Infantino “deceived” staff with his scheme in a damning statement shared with AP, saying they “deserve better than contempt and intimidation.”

Gianni Infantino ally quits as FIFA boss blasted over World Cup plans in angry statement READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino gets fresh reality check as World Cup boycott grows amid calls for change READ MORE :

“It is the project of one person,” Lamour said. “Not only must this project not go ahead … but the time has now come for football political leaders to ask themselves the right questions and make the right decisions.”

Lamour, who also worked with Infantino at UEFA previously, did not resign from his post like Cordeiro but added: “And if that means I lose my job, then so be it. I will understand and respect that decision. At least I’ll sleep well tonight.”

‌



View 2 Images FIFA COO Kevin Lamour has hit out at Infantino and his plans

His comments come hot on the heels of Cordeiro deciding to resign from his post over the plans, which prompted UEFA to confirm their nations will boycott future tournaments if they go ahead.

“I cannot stand by while FIFA considers selling a stake in the World Cup,” Cordeiro said.

Article continues below

“Let me be clear. I had no involvement in this proposal, and I oppose it unequivocally,” he added, describing the proposed $20 billion commercial subsidiary as a “bad deal for football”.

Sports.title: American Affair flies the flag for Goldie at Goodwood
Sports.content:
Scottish speedball American Affair bounced back to form to claim top honours in the King George Qatar Stakes at Goodwood.

Jim Goldie's stable star won the King Charles III Stakes at Royal Ascot last summer, but missed the remainder of the 2025 season through injury.

A second-place finish behind the reopposing Night Raider in Haydock's Temple Stakes in May suggested he retained a good level of his ability, but having trailed home last of all when defending his Ascot title and since come up short in a Listed race at York, he was a 12-1 shot for his latest Group Two assignment.

Always up with the pace in the group that raced closest to the stands rail, American Affair finished off strongly in the hands of his regular partner Paul Mulrennan to get up and beat Rumstar and Time For Sandals down the middle of the track, with Australian raider Asfoora running her best race for a while in fourth.

Goldie senior stayed closer to home, but his son, George, said: "My dad is at Musselburgh, we couldn't both come here, but I think he'll be sorry to have missed out!

"My daughter rides him every day, he's a lovely-natured horse and he's obviously very talented.

"We had faith he'd be back to this level, we've been happy with him at home but things were interrupted by the injury he had at the back end of last year.

"This year it has been a case of building him back up to his best, he showed a glimmer at Haydock three runs ago, but Ascot was a bit of a disaster - he just pulled too hard.

"He ran well at York when he was drawn badly, so we were coming here very hopeful. He's been getting back into that flow of racing properly and finishing his race off.

"We were hoping today was going to suit him better, we were coming here very hopeful."

On future plans, he added: "The plan is to go for the Nunthorpe now, then maybe the Curragh or he could go up to six (furlongs) for the Haydock Sprint Cup.

"We've not entered him in the Abbaye, the Flying Five at the Curragh after the Nunthorpe is more likely."

Weighing-room stalwart Mulrennan said: "He's done everything right today so, touch wood, he comes back from this good. We'll enjoy today, but we've got the Nunthorpe and possibly America would be nice.

"At this stage of the game I've probably got more years behind me than in front of me, but I feel I'm still going strong. It's very competitive, it's hard. I've only got one ride down here this week, but we've made it count.

"I've got my driver with me, Adele (wife). The last time I won it was on Moviesta, Adele drove me then. I've won this race twice and I probably should have won it twice again - Easton Angel probably should have won and Moviesta another year was unlucky, so it's been an unlucky race for me and a lucky race for me, but we got it right today."

Wendy McGrandles of Barraston Racing, who own American Affair with Goldie, said: "He's had one or two excuses and we always felt that he was as good as he was last year. It's once in a lifetime for us, small breeders.

"I remember him as a foal and thinking we could maybe send him eventing if he wasn't fast enough to go racing. He was broken in to go eventing because we weren't sure whether he would be big enough or fast enough to be a racehorse. He can always do that as a second career!"

Burke eyes American trip for Shayem after Thoroughbred success

Karl Burke is eyeing a trip to America with Shayem after he denied the fast-finishing favourite Talk Of New York in the HKJC World Pool Thoroughbred Stakes.

Having finished third behind Wednesday's Sussex Stakes one-two Bow Echo and Gstaad in the St James's Palace at Royal Ascot, this Group Three contest looked a gilt-edged opportunity for Charlie Appleby's Talk Of New York to get back on the winning trail and he was priced up accordingly as the 2-5 market leader.

But while his stablemate Catullus was deployed in a pacemaking role in an attempt to ensure a sound gallop, the favourite was still keen during the early exchanges under William Buick and it then took him a while to find top gear once asked to close the gap.

Karl Burke's Shayem - winner of the Listed Sir Henry Cecil Stakes at Newmarket three weeks ago - was always in the prime position behind Catullus and after grabbing the lead racing inside the final half-furlong, he had enough in hand to keep Talk Of New York at bay by half a length in the hands of Clifford Lee.

"We don't have to lead, but we knew Billy (Loughnane, riding Catullus) was going to go off a nice gallop and Cliff was the only one really to keep tabs on the leader," said Burke.

"Last year, you would have said that he was a soft ground horse but he has proven otherwise this year. We had no qualms about the ground or the track as he handled the undulations at Newmarket well.

"Cliff is very good with his fractions. It was a great performance and Abdulrazaq (Mohamdi, owner) will be delighted as he's a homebred horse as well. He's a great supporter of ours from Dubai.

"There is a nice race at Kentucky Downs for him in September and one at Colonial Downs as well. I don't think they are Grade Ones but they are very valuable races and if if we don't go there, we could come back for the Celebration Mile."

Appleby will let the dust settle on Talk Of New York's disappointing defeat before considering his next move.

He said: "At the top of the hill I thought they'd have to go a bit to go past the lead horse because he's no mug and he likes the track. Stretching to the mile was always going to be the undoing of Catullus - stop the clock a furlong out and we were a comfortable winner.

"William said himself, the front two stole a good march on him and they're two sensible horses. We knew that Catullus was not going to see the mile out eventually but Will said 'I was only just getting rolling there the last furlong'

"I'm not using the track as an excuse, I think the winner is sensible and is improving, he's done everything right, got a nice lead from us and used it, and we've gone and finished the race off.

"You could say do we need to step up in trip? Possibly. But he has got to learn to settle a little bit as well - that first furlong he does want to be a little bit aggressive, but I don't think that was really the undoing of the race to be fair. The pace was on and they weren't coming back at the end of the day."

Sports.title: Doyle: Owen can Dream big in the Stewards' Cup
Sports.content:
Sky Sports Racing ambassador Hollie Doyle reveals her thoughts on the big handicap of the day on Saturday, the Stewards’ Cup at Goodwood.

Dream chance for Owen in Stewards' Cup

Twenty-eight runners rampaging down the hill at Goodwood in one of the most famous handicaps in world racing is a sight to savour and this weekend's Coral Stewards' Cup Handicap (3.35) certainly lives up to expectations.

It's anyone's race but I cannot get away from James Owen's likely favourite Far Above Dream who has the form, the track experience, and the draw in his favour. The four-year-old ran a career-best to finish a close fourth in the Wokingham, just behind his talented stable mate Soldier's Tree, after scoring over this course and distance in May.

He has progressed up the handicap but can race off the same mark as he did at The Royal Meeting and can prove his liking for the cut and thrust of a big field handicap for an upwardly mobile trainer.

All-Weather winner has solid course form

Another on my shortlist for the Stewards' Cup is Ollie Sangster's Tuco Salamanca - an exciting ride for young Irish ace Dylan Browne-McMonagle.

Though his recent wins have been achieved on the All-Weather, including in good company at Newcastle last month, he does have solid course form to his name and has a handy middle draw.

In last weekend's blog I put up Charles Hills's lightly raced seven-year-old Mitbaahy as my 'Hot Shot' so won't be surprised if he makes the frame at big odds on the back of that second in the Group Three Hackwood Stakes at Newbury.

Star to deny Waardah a second win in Langtry

Santorini Star has the class and the constitution to add the Group Two Qatar Lillie Langtry Stakes (3.00) on Saturday to her Group Two victories in the Park Hill Stakes at Doncaster and the Jockey Club Stakes at Newmarket.

William Haggas's five-year-old had a rare blip in the Hardwicke Stakes at Royal Ascot but this is an ideal assignment for a mare who stays well and, crucially, has winning form at the track.

Her closest market rival will be the Owen Burrows-trained Waardah, who won this race last year and found only subsequent Group One Pretty Polly Stakes Winner Estrange too good in a Group Three at Carlisle last time. She is entitled to come on for her first outing since last Autumn, but Santorini Star's overall profile is more compelling.

Three in a row for veteran Al Aasy

William Haggas holds the key to the Group Three Coral Glorious Stakes (2.25) on Saturday with market leaders Al Aasy and Opportunity, but I am expecting the veteran to win this race for the third year in a row.

Tom (Marquand) will be looking to smuggle him into the race, just as Jim Crowley did 12 months ago, and can expect another committed performance from Shadwell's wonderful Sea The Stars gelding.

Seemingly as good as ever and proven on the track, he can get the better of Wathnan Racing's Duke Of Edinburgh Stakes hero Opportunity who took his form to a new level at Royal Ascot but needs to find more on this step back into Group company.

O'Brien gelding can build on Royal Ascot form

Godolphin's Valedictory will be well supported in the Highclere Castle Gin Summer Handicap (1.50) on Saturday, and rightly so, but I am taking him on with Irish raider Aeronautic, who can improve on his third in the race last year.

Joseph O'Brien's five-year-old struck me as a winner waiting to happen when finishing fourth in the Copper Horse Stakes at the Royal Meeting. He hasn't won for a long time but has proven he can be highly competitive off this mark of 97.

Valedictory won over course and distance in May when he was transformed by the cheekpieces but a three-pound rise for a narrow win at Newmarket last time demands more from John and Thady Gosden's gelding.

Another to consider is Charlie Johnston's Northumberland Plate Victor Align The Stars who took this prize two years ago but has never won off a triple digit rating.

Time for talented Jack to shine

Promising apprentice Jack Nicholls can make a name for himself in the Phase Eight Handicap (4.10) on Saturday when he partners Naval Light for his in-form boss Karl Burke.

The three-year-old carries a relatively low weight and Jack's three-pound claim can give him a decisive edge in this higher grade following wins at Pontefract and Catterick this summer.

Startled has been running well for Richard Hughes who has enlisted another talented claimer in Harry Vigors for this assignment. He looks fairly treated on his course and distance second in May so should be in the mix.

Billy was just brilliant on stunning Echo

Bow Echo produced the performance of the week at the Qatar Goodwood Festival, showing a blistering turn of foot to win the Group One Visit Qatar Sussex Stakes (4.10, Wednesday) and extend his unbeaten record to six.

He's clearly a very special talent - a comment that applies to his young jockey Billy Loughnane, who has shown a maturity beyond his years on George Boughey's superstar.

It takes a special horse to get out of the kind of difficult situation he found himself in on the Downs but a top-class jockey to execute a victory as Billy did so coolly. It was a great ride that will live long in the memory of racing fans and one I thoroughly enjoyed watching.

Oxygen chamber is helping my recovery

Since coming out of hospital following my fall in May, I've been using a hyperbaric oxygen chamber which we've had installed at home, and the results are encouraging.

The chamber basically increases air pressure to deliver pure one hundred per cent oxygen into your bloodstream which helps with healing. Sitting in there for an hour a day has become part of my rehabilitation routine now.

I'm also continuing with my gym programme and physiotherapy at Oaksey House in Lambourn five days a week but still don't have any idea of a comeback date at this stage.

Sports.title: Newcastle to appoint Jaissle as new boss tomorrow after Howe exit confirmed
Sports.content:
Newcastle are set to announce Matthias Jaissle as their new head coach on Saturday after Eddie Howe's exit was confirmed.

Sky Sports News can reveal Newcastle have agreed to pay £9.5m (€11m) compensation to Saudi side Al Ahli for Jaissle.

The German, who previously managed Red Bull Salzburg, will sign a four-year contract at St James' Park.

The plan is for the 38-year-old to meet up with his new players in Spain on Saturday at their training camp in La Manga.

Jaissle's imminent appointment comes after Newcastle officially announced Howe's departure on Friday, a day after Sky Sports News had revealed his exit.

The reason the Howe statement was held up was to allow the club to ensure the Jaissle deal was agreed.

Jaissle's first match in charge will be a pre-season friendly against Valencia at the Mestalla next Saturday.

Howe steps down 'to recharge and take a break'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie Redknapp backs former Newcastle head coach Eddie Howe to get back into management at a 'top club'.

Howe says managing Newcastle has been the privilege of his life after confirming he had stepped down as head coach.

The 48-year-old ended the Magpies' 70-year wait for domestic silverware with Carabao Cup glory in 2025, as well as overseeing qualification for the Champions League twice.

The Premier League club confirmed his exit on Friday afternoon, saying they had accepted his decision to step down and thanked him for his "extraordinary contribution".

Departing Howe said in a lengthy statement: "After a period of personal reflection, I have decided that now is the right time for me to step away from my role as head coach of Newcastle United.

"After nearly five years of giving my life, heart and soul into the club with unrelenting energy, I feel that it is in the best interests of both myself and the club to step away, recharge and take a break.

"Although it's been incredibly difficult to make this decision, I know in my heart that it's the right one. I have always put the best interests of Newcastle before my own in every single decision I have made whilst I've been here and this one is no different.

"It has been the privilege of my lifetime to have been the manager of Newcastle United.

"It is difficult to put into words what this club, the city and its supporters mean, and will always mean, to me and my family."

Howe's heartfelt 547-word message reflected on the highs and lows of his time in the north east, where he created memories that he will "cherish for the rest of my life".

Newcastle chief executive David Hopkinson added: "Eddie and his staff leave with the deep gratitude and respect of everyone at Newcastle United, and with a lasting place in the club's history.

"While we are naturally disappointed to see Eddie leave, we remain immensely thankful for everything he has done for the club.

"On behalf of our owners, board, players, staff and supporters, I would like to extend sincere thanks to Eddie for his outstanding service and leadership, and wish him and his family every success and happiness for the future."

Howe is followed out of St James' Park by coaches Jason Tindall, Graeme Jones, Stephen Purches and Simon Weatherstone, as well as head of performance Dan Hodges.

'King of this club!' - Guimaraes posts Howe farewell message

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie Redknapp believes Bruno Guimaraes can benefit from Eddie Howe leaving Newcastle

Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes has called Howe the 'king of this club' following the head coach's exit.

Howe's resignation comes amid Arsenal's interest in Guimaraes, who has praised his former boss.

In an Instagram post, Guimaraes wrote the words over a picture of Howe: "King of this club!!

"Thanks for everything you've done for us. I loved enjoying our time together. Thanks for making me a better player and person!

"No words I can say will really say how much I enjoyed being your player. "Wish you all the very best in your future, gaffer."

Hornicek to be first-choice goalkeeper after £25.7m deal agreed

Image: Lukas Hornicek is set to join Newcastle from Braga

Newcastle have an agreement in principle with Braga for Lukas Hornicek, who is being brought in to be the club's first-choice goalkeeper.

Newcastle have agreed to activate his £25.7m (€30m) release clause, and are now discussing payment terms with the Portuguese club.

The 24-year-old Czech has been given permission to travel for a medical, as the two clubs tie up the loose ends of a deal.

He will become their fifth signing of the summer, taking the spending to £140m.

Sports.title: Chelsea's Mudryk cleared to play after doping ban resolved
Sports.content:
Chelsea winger Mykhailo Mudryk has been cleared to return to play after his doping ban was resolved.

The 25-year-old has not played competitively since November 2024 after he was suspended for four years for failing a drug test, which revealed the presence of a low concentration of meldonium, a prohibited substance, two years ago.

Mudryk filed an appeal with the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) while changes to World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) procedures in the interim mean that had his failed test produced the same result now, charges would not have been brought.

The FA said: "Changes have been made… which, while not retroactive, mean that if Mr Mudryk's sample was collected today, the concentration of meldonium in the sample would not have been reported and no anti-doping rule violations would have resulted.

"Further to that development and to other circumstances of the case, the FA and Mr Mudryk have now - with the agreement of WADA - resolved the appeal proceedings.

"As a part of the agreement, Mr Mudryk accepted that he had committed the ADRVs (Anti-Doping Rule Violations) charged and acceded to a period of ineligibility equal to the time served at the date of the agreement.

"Mr Mudryk is no longer ineligible and may return to competition with immediate effect."

The Blues signed Mudryk for £88m from Shakhtar Donetsk in January 2023 and made 73 appearances, scoring nine goals, before his ban.

Chelsea welcomed the decision and said they will support his "reintegration into the squad" while "helping him resume his career".

A Chelsea statement said: "We welcome the acknowledgement that advances in the applicable scientific reporting standards for more reliable testing mean that, had Misha's sample been analysed under today's technical requirements, it would not have been reported as a positive test and no anti-doping rule violation would have resulted. That is an important part of the context surrounding the agreed resolution and allows everyone involved to move forward."

The Ukraine international also released a statement in which he said his two years away from football have "been the most difficult period of my career" and that he was "grateful" to be able to return.

Mudryk's charity shop work during ban - but will he play for Blues this season?

Sky Sports News' Kaveh Solhekol:

Mudryk believed his sample, which tested positive for heart drug meldonium, was contaminated when he was on international duty with Ukraine in October 2024.

He tested positive during a period when Ukraine played in Albania and Georgia in November 2024 before then being provisionally suspended by the FA a month later.

Mudryk has always maintained his innocence and had been keeping fit by working with his own personal trainers away from Chelsea's Cobham training ground.

In fact, he was recently spotted working in a charity shop in London. Mudryk has not been allowed to train at Chelsea's Cobham training ground.

It now remains to be seen whether Mudryk will be part of Xabi Alonso's squad this season.

Chelsea have the option of sending him on loan to regain full match fitness.

Sports.title: 'Lighten up!' - Hull responds to caddie prank criticism during major push
Sports.content:
Charley Hull insists she 'does not care' about criticism over her pre-major caddie prank and overcame limited sleep to remain firmly in AIG Women's Open title contention.

Hull followed an opening-round 69 with a level-par 71 on Friday morning at Royal Lytham & St Annes, mixing three birdies with as many bogeys to head into the weekend on two under and in contention in the final major of the year.

She faced scrutiny on social media after admitting pre-tournament that she tricked her caddie Adam Woodward into thinking he'd won £100,000 on a scratchcard, capturing the moment on camera after purchasing the fake ticket in a Blackpool joke shop.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hull reveals the hilarious scratchcard prank she pulled on her caddie Adam Woodward ahead of the AIG Women's Open.

Hull insists she was unaffected by the negative comments and that her caddie embraced the 'banter', with the world No 7 now fully focused on making a weekend charge and challenging for an elusive major victory.

"I don't think people understand mine and Adsy's [Woodward, caddie] relationship," Hull said post-round. "We're very, very close. He's like a big brother to me. He is one of my best friends.

"He's always taking the mickey out of me. He thought the joke was brilliant himself - he was showing everybody about it and he was laughing hard about it. Then when you hear comments, so many people saying how bad it is, I'm like 'just lighten up'.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hull holed a bunker shot for birdie at the 17th hole to close on clubhouse leader Shiho Kuwaki

"I don't care if you don't get my humour - my friends get my humour and that's why they're my friends. I wouldn't do it to a random person that I knew wouldn't take it very well.

"We all know Adsy is the king of pranks. The amount of pranks he and his caddie mates are just way worse than that, and he just finds it hilarious. He's pretty chill and people need to chill out about that. Adsy is loving the attention from it!

"He texted me last night saying this has been one of the funniest weeks ever because of that prank, so people need to stop writing bad comments and stuff because they need to lighten up. If you got something bad to say about it, I don't care!"

Image: Charley Hull with caddie Adam Woodward during the AIG Women's Open

When asked how Hull responds to negative comments, she added: "They actually make me want to do better because I think we live in a world where you can't do anything wrong these days, and then it stops people from living the life they want to.

"I don't care - I just live me. Our household has a lot of banter and are always taking the mickey out of each other. It's just the way I've been brought up, and I think people just need to be a bit more tough-skinned.

"I think you put yourself in the limelight so you would be silly to think there will not be comments like that. I think you see some people saying I really struggle from these comments and they're almost looking for sympathy.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking ahead of the tournament, Hull claims she doesn't see Nelly Korda as her rival due to the fact she's yet to lift a major title

"I'm just like 'you're in such a good position in life. There are people way worse off in life and you're moaning about what people are saying about you'. I just think grow a pair of balls and just forget about it, do you know what I mean?

"If that's the worst thing in life, people saying bad stuff about you, you really have not got life that bad."

Hull admitted she only had around three hours' sleep ahead of her second round, with the Englishwoman - a five-time major runner-up who has finished second twice in the last three years at this event - ready for the challenge ahead.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hull holed a bunker shot for birdie at the 17th hole to close on clubhouse leader Shiho Kuwaki

"Really looking forward to it," Hull said. "It's going to be loads of fun. I feel like now my nerves have settled down. My back was actually playing up for me a little bit today, a little bit sore, that's why I think I wasn't getting through the ball how I wanted to.

"Not too far back going into the weekend - better than I was last year!"

Who will win the AIG Women's Open? Watch throughout the weekend live on Sky Sports. Live coverage continues Saturday from midday on Sky Sports Golf. Get Sky Sports or stream golf and more with no contract.

Sports.title: Chelsea handed £10m fine and suspended transfer ban
Sports.content:
Chelsea have been fined £10m and given a suspended two-window transfer ban by an independent appeal board after admitting breaches of Football Association agent rules, the FA has announced.

An earlier independent commission had imposed a suspended six-point deduction, which was set aside and the suspended transfer ban imposed in its place.

The FA confirmed the imposition of sanctions on the west London club on Friday, who admitted to a total of 74 breaches of FA regulations covering agents, working with intermediaries and third-party investment in players.

The club's new owners self-reported the breaches to the football authorities in May 2022, when they were in the process of buying the club from Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich.

The transfers which raised potential concerns during the takeover process are believed to include deals for players such as Eden Hazard, Samuel Eto'o and Willian. There is no suggestion of any wrongdoing on the part of those players.

The six-point deduction, suspended until June 30 2027, was imposed by the independent commission which initially heard the case but the club appealed against that. An appeal board instead replaced the points penalty with the suspended two-window transfer ban.

The £10m fine imposed by the Regulatory Commission was not subject to appeal and the full amount will be invested into grassroots football.

Chelsea have previously entered sanction settlements in regard to this matter with the Premier League and UEFA.

A club statement read: "Chelsea Football Club is pleased to confirm that a final decision has been reached by The FA's judicial bodies in relation to historical regulatory matters that were self-reported by the club.

"In 2022, the club self-reported potential historical rule breaches to all applicable regulators. Following that report, it has worked openly and transparently with all regulators, including voluntarily and proactively disclosing many thousands of documents.

Image: The payments were made under former Chelsea owner Roman Abramovich

"As previously announced, settlement agreements have been entered into with UEFA and the Premier League concerning the same self-reported regulatory matters and topics that have been addressed before. The club is pleased to confirm that, now The FA process has concluded, this brings all regulatory proceedings against the club to a close.

"We are grateful to UEFA, the Premier League and The FA for their engagement with the club throughout these processes."

Earlier this year, Chelsea were handed the Premier League's biggest fine along with a one-year transfer ban, suspended for two years. The total fine of £10.75m related to secret payments made to agents worth £47.5m between 2011 and 2018, when Roman Abramovich was owner, and breaches of rules around registering youth players.

The total fine was going to be £20m but it was halved because the Blues self-reported and co-operated with the investigation.

The Premier League report named a number of transfers related to the secret payments, including deals for Hazard, Eto'o, Willian, Ramires, David Luiz, Andre Schurrle and Nemanja Matic. The names of four players were redacted in the report.

Image: Former Chelsea forward Eden Hazard was among the players mentioned in various offences, although there is no indication of wrongdoing from the player himself

Clubs must provide the FA and Premier League accurate financial information every year. The same applies for UEFA and clubs playing in their competition.

Chelsea were fined £8.64m by UEFA in July 2023 for incomplete financial reporting by the previous owners in 2018 and 2019. At least six suspect payments to offshore companies connected to transfers were identified.

'Some fans may be thinking Chelsea have got off lightly'

Analysis from Sky Sports News' Kaveh Solhekol:

"On one hand, it's not good news for Chelsea because they've been hit with a fine and a suspended transfer ban, but I imagine a lot of people who are not Chelsea supporters will be thinking 'Chelsea have got off lightly, they really should have got a points deduction'.

"I'm sure fans of clubs who have been hit with points deductions in the past will be saying 'why did we get real punishments that affected our seasons when Chelsea are just getting a financial penalty which their owners can afford to pay?'

"Chelsea have been fined three times for offences that came to light and were reported by the new owners.

"Having said that, when you read stories and opinion on this, people feel Chelsea have got off lightly, but I'm sure their supporters and owners would say 'we got fined by UEFA, the Premier League and the FA. We've been punished three times for the same offences that we didn't commit. It was the previous ownership'."

Sports.title: Infantino under huge pressure after plan for World Cup sell-off sparks resignation and rebuke
Sports.content:
The walls started closing in on Gianni Infantino after another dramatic day that saw one of his senior advisers resign and brought a scathing rebuke from Fifa’s own chief operating officer.

Infantino is under huge pressure after his plan to sell chunks of the World Cup to private investors met a tide of opposition from around the globe. European countries have already promised to boycott Fifa competitions if he does not shelve the scheme but Friday’s developments, which led to two key members of his inner circle distancing themselves from him, may prove equally damaging to any prospects of salvaging his presidency.

Meanwhile Uefa and other confederations are actively seeking candidates to run against Infantino in next year’s Fifa election, in which he had been expected to comfortably win a fourth term. The pressure that has built since this week’s revelations casts doubt on whether the previously unassailable Swiss, who has doubled down on the proposals, will be able to cling on for that long.

The resignation of Carlos Cordeiro, one of Infantino’s senior advisers since 2021, struck a fresh blow upon Infantino hours after Uefa’s 55 members had unanimously threatened a boycott. Cordeiro, a former US Soccer chief, said Infantino had proposed “a bad deal for Fifa’s member associations, a bad deal for football, and a bad deal for the long-term future of the game”. He questioned the lack of transparency in Fifa’s process and pointed out that the governing body is sitting on vast debt-free reserves that could be used to fund development.

“Why this deal?” he asked. “Why now? What oversight exists? Who benefits? Was there a competitive process? What governance will be in place? What will investors ultimately gain, and at what cost to football?”

But an extraordinary statement later in the day by Kevin Lamour, Fifa’s current chief operating officer, may have inflicted a more serious wound. Lamour, a close associate of Infantino at Fifa and during their previous spells at Uefa, said staff and other stakeholders had been “deceived” by the president and said he would tolerate being sacked for expressing his views.

double quotation mark We all want to be proud to work for Fifa, and today, unfortunately, it seems that is no longer the case for many of us Kevin Lamour, Fifa chief operating officer

“What has been announced in recent days and what has been happening behind the scenes in recent months defies belief and imagination,” Lamour said. “To put it very clearly and directly: the project that has sparked so much controversy and debate is not a Fifa project. It is even less a project of Fifa’s administration. It is the project of one person.

“The Fifa vice-presidents, the members of the Fifa Council, the confederations, the federations, the players, the leagues, the clubs, and the fans were not the only ones who were ignored. Fifa’s own administration was also deceived.

“This lie by omission over many months and this unilateral exercise of power are not trivial. They are indicative of a lack of trust, a lack of transparency, a lack of discernment, a lack of good governance. And a serious lack of respect.”

Lamour said Fifa’s mission is “not to serve the personal interests of a person who, unfortunately, believes he embodies Fifa when he is supposed to be at its service”. He stated that his colleagues “deserve better than contempt and intimidation”, adding: “My feeling is that we all want to be proud to work for Fifa, and today, unfortunately, it seems that is no longer the case for many of us.”

Infantino appears to be shedding allies and there was no succour to be taken from a strongly worded statement from the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), which backed Uefa and Concacaf in their opposition to the privately funded Fifa Forward Enterprise plan. The AFC stopped short of matching Uefa’s boycott but was clear in saying the proposal should be scrapped.

View image in fullscreen Carlos Cordeiro (left) with Donald Trump and Gianni Infantino in the Oval Office in 2018. Photograph: Evan Vucci/AP

“The fact that the situation has reached the point where the real possibility of a Fifa World Cup boycott has entered public discourse should concern everyone who cares about the future of our game,” it said. “The AFC believes that the proposed FFE cannot realistically achieve the necessary broad consensus and unity required to move forward.”

It called upon Fifa to “undertake an urgent review of its governance and decision-making framework”, echoing its peers’ complaints about a lack of consultation regarding key decisions such as World Cup hosting arrangements.

A further revelation on Friday that Fifa has opened a tender for research companies to assess the economic benefits of expanding the World Cup to 64 teams, demanding a hugely accelerated timescale, has only increased such concerns in football’s corridors of power.

Uefa is minded to play a waiting game after securing a united front in opposing Infantino’s plan. It will assess how Fifa reacts, although early signs suggest little change of tack. Overnight Fifa had attempted to blame media reporting for such widespread opposition, claiming its commitment to “an open and democratic consultation”, although that intervention has cut no ice among its opponents.

It is unlikely any mechanism to depose Infantino will be triggered immediately although in theory an extraordinary Fifa Congress, and subsequent vote of confidence, could be convened if 43 countries make such a request. The priority around Uefa and beyond is to see off the FFE plan before taking further steps. Any Europe-backed candidate for the Fifa presidency election in March is likely to hail from a different continent, with the Concacaf president, Victor Montagliani, and AFC president, Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim al-Khalifa, among possible contenders. The latter lost narrowly to Infantino in the 2016 election.

Fifa continues to lobby federations to accept their project and have stuck by the 19 September deadline originally given for those who wish to sign up.

Sports.title: Inter make new approach to Liverpool for Curtis Jones with £30m offer likely
Sports.content:
Inter have made another approach for Curtis Jones and are willing to raise their offer for the Liverpool midfielder to €35m (£30m). The Italian champions had a €25m bid for the 25-year-old rejected in June by Liverpool, who value their homegrown player at closer to €40m.

Intermediaries representing Inter have made fresh contact with Liverpool this week and outlined their willingness to go to €35m for a player who has only one year remaining on his contract at Anfield. Whether Liverpool accept that sum is doubtful, but a deal for Jones to leave his boyhood club does appear to be edging closer.

Jones has been unable to establish himself as a regular starter at Liverpool and cut a frustrated figure at times last season under Arne Slot. He was also involved in a row with Dominik Szoboszlai after Wednesday’s win over Wrexham in New York, seemingly over not being handed the captain’s armband when Szoboszlai was substituted during the second half of the friendly.

The new Liverpool head coach, Andoni Iraola, has spoken of the importance of keeping Jones and a local identity at the start of his first season in charge but Inter’s determination to sign the England international, along with the prospect of losing him for free next summer, may well test that resolve.

Sports.title: Arsenal target Bruno Guimarães not on Newcastle’s flight to pre-season camp
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimarães was not on Newcastle’s flight to Murcia on Friday lunchtime as Eddie Howe’s former players prepared to meet their new head coach in southern Spain.

As Guimarães, who is believed to be in Brazil, appeared to inch closer towards a transfer to Arsenal, Matthias Jaissle was completing his managerial move from Saudi Arabia’s Al-Ahli. Howe’s successor is expected to arrive at the club’s pre-season training camp at La Manga at some point this weekend.

By the time, shortly after midday, when the team’s charter plane took off for the Mediterranean, Newcastle had still to provide formal confirmation of Howe’s departure. That did not arrive until late afternoon but it is understood they had been negotiating a financial settlement with their former manager in addition to payoffs for four key members of his backroom staff, including the outgoing No 2, Jason Tindall.

In an emotional message released as part of Newcastle’s statement, Howe said. “It has been the privilege of my lifetime to have been the manager of Newcastle United. After nearly five years of giving my life, heart and soul into this club with unrelenting energy I feel that it is in the best interests of both myself and the club to step away, recharge and take a break. Although it’s been incredibly difficult to make this decision, I know in my heart it’s the right one.”

The amicable nature of the parting was reflected in generous tributes paid by Newcastle’s chief executive David Hopkinson, sporting director Ross Wilson and minority owner, Jamie Reuben. The latter said: “I am proud to have worked alongside Eddie Howe and privileged to call him a friend.” Hopkinson said: “Eddie and his staff leave with the deep gratitude and respect of everyone at Newcastle United and a lasting place in the club’s history.”

Although Howe had told Newcastle of his intention to leave earlier this month, leaks surrounding Jaissle’s imminent installation appeared to catch all parties by surprise. The players had learned of their manager’s departure during a day off on Thursday but had the situation fully explained when Wilson addressed them at the training ground before heading to Spain alongside the squad.

At the same time, Newcastle’s incoming German head coach was understood to be finalising a four-year contract at St James’ Park after an £8m compensation package was agreed with Al-Ahli. Jaissle is already in Europe after remaining in Portugal rather than returning to Jeddah with his squad following the conclusion of a pre-season training camp on the Algarve on Wednesday.

View image in fullscreen Joelinton could be on his way to the Saudi Arabia league this summer. Photograph: Siu Wu/EPA

The 38-year-old former RB Salzburg manager is assembling his own backroom staff and now has only three weeks before his first Premier League season begins with a home game against Liverpool.

One of his first tasks will be to hold talks with Guimarães regarding the Brazil midfielder’s future. Guimarães – who was very close to Howe – is booked on a flight to Spain on Sunday but there are suggestions he could opt to board a London-bound plane instead, should Arsenal offer Newcastle a sum in the region of £75m.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Although Manchester United are exploring the possibility of signing Lewis Hall, Jaissle has reason to be more confident of keeping the influential left back. Newcastle are said to be determined to retain one of their best young players but could be more receptive to any bid from Saudi Arabia for Joelinton. Guimarães’s fellow Brazilian is believed to be keen on a move to the Middle East.

While Besiktas also covet another Newcastle midfielder, Joe Willock, Wilson appears close to securing a new goalkeeper. A £26m deal for the Braga and Czechia goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek is expected to be completed over the weekend.

Should that move for the 24-year-old progress as planned, Nick Pope, Newcastle’s current first-choice keeper, will almost certainly prove yet another departure during a turbulent summer featuring a major changing of the guard on Tyneside.

Sports.title: Arsenal’s next step: title defence may hinge on keeping a drained squad fit
Sports.content:
After beating MK Dons 3-0 in a training-ground friendly last weekend, Arsenal truly begin their pre-season programme against Girona on Saturday evening. It marks a return to action for the Premier League champions, who will want to show their success last season was not a one-off.

Retaining the English title is incredibly difficult if you are not Manchester City. No other club has done it since Manchester United won three in succession from 2007 to 2009. Chelsea have done it once, Liverpool have not managed it for more than 40 years, and it is the best part of a century since Arsenal retained the crown. Mikel Arteta faces a sizeable challenge.

Reaching a second successive Champions League final will not be simple either. Manchester City in 2021-22 are the only one of England’s previous five finalists who made it as far as the semi-finals the next season. With the Premier League stronger than ever, competing on two fronts has never been tougher. Transfer business may improve Arsenal’s chances, though their spending has been modest to this point. More than half of the £79m spent was on making Piero Hincapié’s loan permanent.

Elsewhere Arsenal have replaced Leandro Trossard with Christos Tzolis, a Greek winger, from Club Brugge. Seven years younger than the Belgian, his arrival is a logical move in future-proofing the squad. However, the left side of Arsenal’s attack would be elevated to truly elite level if they could secure reported target Vinícius Júnior. The on-field argument speaks for itself. Vinícius made 92 carries of at least five metres that ended with him either taking a shot (49) or creating a chance (43) last season, the most of anyone in Europe’s top five leagues. Open-play threat, for a side that has often relied on set pieces, would be considerably increased.

Those holding the purse strings at Arsenal may have pause for thought. Capology’s wage data estimates that Vinícius is the joint-third highest paid player in Europe’s top five leagues, earning in excess of £100,000 a week more than anyone at his potential new club. Would Arsenal be willing to rewrite their wage structure? They should expect calls from the agents of their current players if they are. In this sense, Bradley Barcola, with whom they have also been linked, makes a more plausible target. The issue there would be competition from Liverpool, who are in far greater need of wingers.

This is the test facing Andrea Berta, Arsenal’s sporting director. Improving a squad that is already one of the best around is not easy. When Berta’s arrived last year, the club’s primary targets were said to be Alexander Isak and Benjamin Sesko, both of whom joined rivals instead. The pool of players who could add something significant to Arteta’s options is drying up.

Keeping existing players fit may be more beneficial than enhancing the squad. Arsenal did well to win the league given only a handful of clubs had players that missed more games. Kai Havertz was reportedly their top earner before Bukayo Saka signed a contract extension in February, but he only started seven league games. The captain, Martin Ødegaard, was also unavailable for spells, meaning he and Saka started only 10 Premier League matches together in 2025-26. One of them coincided with the only game for which Declan Rice was injured (the 4-1 home win over Aston Villa), another (another home win, 2-1 against Brighton) when he started at right-back.

View image in fullscreen Mikel Arteta indulges in a bit of training-ground banter with first-team coach Miguel Molina in Girona. Photograph: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC/Getty Images

This meant Arteta was rarely able to give key men a breather. Arsenal have five of the Premier League’s top 20 players for club minutes in all competitions since the start of last season. Granted, the goalkeeper David Raya is one of them. But their outfield players with more than 4,200 minutes were Rice (4,456 minutes, the 11th most for a Premier League club), Martín Zubimendi (4,298, 15th), William Saliba (4,254, 17th) and Gabriel Magalhães (4,210, 19th), all vital components of the side’s spine.

Saliba also played 795 minutes for France, pushing him past 5,000 minutes before his World Cup was prematurely ended by a back injury that looks likely to sideline him for some time. It is remarkable Rice was able to play 1,026 minutes for England on top of his Arsenal commitments, not least as he has managed nerve pain in a hamstring throughout 2026.

This workload clearly impacted his ability to contribute at his best for Thomas Tuchel this summer, and that will be a concern for Arteta. With Viktor Gyökeres also clocking up plenty of playing time for Sweden, Arsenal have six players with at least 4,400 minutes for club and country since the start of last August.

This may have been a factor in Arsenal opting for a relatively low-key pre-season. They visited Asia last summer, but the trip to Catalonia to play Girona is the furthest they will travel this year. Arsenal also have games in Dublin (against Real Betis) and Cardiff (the Community Shield against City) sandwiching home friendlies against Borussia Dortmund and Como.

With players still recovering from their World Cup exertions, it may be some time before we see the true Arsenal. A combination of fatigue, injuries and potential squad additions means the process could take far longer than would be ideal.

Sports.title: Chelsea fined £10m and given suspended transfer ban by FA over agent breaches
Sports.content:
Chelsea have been fined £10m by the FA and served with a suspended transfer ban for multiple violations of transfer rules during the Roman Abramovich era.

The sanction reflects a similar punishment handed to the Blues by the Premier League earlier this year after the club were found to have used unlicensed agents and sought to obscure the nature of their transfer dealings between 2009 and 2022. Deals involving Chelsea legends Samuel Eto’o, Eden Hazard and Willian were among those found to have breached the rules. The commission originally handed down a stronger sanction that would have given Chelsea a suspended six-point deduction, but it was overturned after an appeal by the club.

The offences were self-reported by Chelsea when new ownership entered Stamford Bridge in 2022 and the disciplinary panel praised the club for their actions and cooperation through the hearing. Chelsea, who are also operating under a settlement agreement with Uefa, said they had “worked openly and transparently with all regulators” and were “pleased to confirm that this brings all regulatory proceedings against the club to a close”.

Written reasons published by the FA show the independent commission took a very dim view of the Abramovich-era administration, saying their rule-breaking showed “a shameful and arrogant disregard for the rules of the game … which has done so much to bring the game of football in general, and the name of CFC into disrepute”. They also said, however, that there were aspects of the case brought by the FA that caused them “particular concern”.

While praising the FA’s cooperation on the case, the commission criticised the governing body for both failing to charge individuals related to the misdemeanours and for requesting that a sporting sanction should not be applied as punishment. After a submission by the Premier League, which also argued against a sporting sanction, Chelsea appealed against the commission’s original sanction and the six-point deduction was replaced with a suspended two-window ban on registering new players. While the commission had originally argued Chelsea had sought and gained a sporting advantage from their actions, the appeal board found that there was insufficient evidence to show that any advantage had actually been achieved.

“Chelsea’s lawyers performed a masterclass in non-adversarial diplomacy with both the FA and the Premier League,” said Stefan Borson, a football finance expert who is head of sport at the law firm McCarthy Denning.

“Even where the FA’s independent panel disagreed with the position presented by the FA and Chelsea, it still found a way to discount a 15-point deduction starting point down to a six-point suspended penalty. Ultimately, even that was appealed away, leaving Chelsea to pay a final meagre fine out of its retained escrow from Abramovich’s proceeds.”

Quick Guide Mudryk cleared to resume playing Show Chelsea winger Mykhailo Mudryk can return to playing immediately after the Football Association and the World Anti-Doping Agency “resolved his appeal” against a ban for failing a doping test. The Ukrainian was suspended for four years after failing a drug test which revealed the presence of a low concentration of meldonium, a prohibited substance, in 2024. Mudryk filed an appeal with the Court of Arbitration for Sport while changes to Wada procedures in the interim mean that had his failed test produced the same result now, charges would not have been brought. The FA said: “Changes have been made … which, while not retroactive, mean that if Mr Mudryk’s sample was collected today, the concentration of meldonium in the sample would not have been reported and no anti-doping rule violations [ADRVs] would have resulted. Further to that development and to other circumstances of the case, the FA and Mr Mudryk have now – with the agreement of Wada – resolved the appeal proceedings. “As a part of the agreement, Mr Mudryk accepted that he had committed the ADRVs charged and acceded to a period of ineligibility equal to the time served at the date of the agreement. Mr Mudryk is no longer ineligible and may return to competition with immediate effect.” PA Media Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

The Premier League and the FA had been examining tens of millions of pounds in secret payments made by offshore companies that were owned by Abramovich. Details of the transactions were uncovered as part of Cyprus Confidential, an investigation by the Guardian and international media partners, based on a leak of data from Cypriot financial services firms that the Russian oligarch used to manage his vast fortunes.

Deals revealed by the leak included apparent off-book payments to Hazard’s agent and an associate of the title-winning manager Antonio Conte.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Documents published as part of the finding offer a rare insight into the inner workings of Chelsea’s transfer policy during the tenure of Abramovich. They refer to internal conversations at Chelsea about the purchase of Willian in 2013, a deal agreed at the last minute, after the Brazilian had apparently been set to join London rivals Tottenham. According to the documents, an unnamed senior figure at Chelsea felt that to lose Willian was “not good” and that to lose him to Tottenham was “adding insult to injury”.

In its argument, the FA said the unnamed individual may have “loved the power associated with having a bottomless pocket when it came to acquiring players of great quality and/or with great potential, but to seek to suggest that there was no intention to obtain a sporting advantage is stretching our credulity beyond reasonable limits”.

The rulings published by the FA also reveal for the first time that BlueCo, the consortium that bought Chelsea from Abramovich, reached a multi-million pound settlement with HM Revenue & Customs relating to transactions dating back to 2011. The size of the settlement is redacted in the FA’s case against Chelsea but the appeal board’s decision indicated that the club repaid at least £1.35m.

The FA said that the entirety of Chelsea’s £10m fine will be invested into grassroots football.

Sports.title: Who should win the men’s Ballon d’Or?
Sports.content:
Harry Kane

Seventy-three goals in 64 games for club and country – the second most prolific season by any player in history after Lionel Messi’s 82-goal campaign in 2011-12 – not bad for a man who once sat on the bench alongside Jamie Vardy in the Championship. Harry Kane was not a teenage prodigy like a few of the other players on this list but here he is crashing football’s top table at the age of 33.

It feels strange that a player who has scored at least 24 goals in each of the last 12 seasons, has won back-to-back Golden Boots in the Premier League, a World Cup Golden Boot and two European Golden Shoes, has never finished higher than 10th in Ballon d’Or voting.

The numbers were always there but now he is adding the silverware. Kane’s trophy drought ended when Bayern Munich won the Bundesliga last year and that triumph has opened the floodgates. Another Bundesliga title followed this season, alongside the DFB-Pokal and German Supercup.

England did not end their trophy drought at the World Cup but their captain scored six goals and overtook Gary Lineker as England’s top scorer at the tournament, ensuring he remained in contention for the Ballon d’Or.

Lamine Yamal

“It’s about being calm. When I’m in the area with the ball, I decide what happens,” said Lamine Yamal in February after he had scored the first hat-trick of his career in Barcelona’s 4-1 win against Villarreal. For most 19-year-olds this would sound like arrogance, but Yamal is not like most 19-year-olds.

He offered more proof of that this summer. The Spain forward became the first player to appear in a European Championship final and a World Cup final before turning 20 – and he won both. He only scored one goal at the World Cup, which was a modest return by his own lofty standards, but he was influential throughout. He won a gamechanging penalty in the semi-final against France, he made more successful take-ons than Messi across the tournament, and he had a hand in breaking down an Argentina side hellbent on baiting him into a physical duel in the final. He achieved all this after going into the tournament with a hamstring injury. Joe Hart captured the mood best after the final, saying: “Lamine Yamal is 19 years old. What a beautiful day for him. He’s 19 and has completed football.”

Add in the 24 goals and 18 assists he racked up in 45 appearances for Barcelona as they won La Liga and the Supercopa, and he has a strong case to go one better than his runners-up finish in last year’s Ballon d’Or.

Rodri

“We’ll see the real Rodri at the World Cup,” said Pep Guardiola last October, when the Manchester City captain returned to action after suffering an ACL injury. There were doubts that the 2023 Ballon d’Or winner would ever return to his best. But, as with most things in football, Guardiola was right.

Rodri was the heartbeat and the safety blanket in the Spain team, dictating every phase of the game, controlling possession and extinguishing almost every danger posed to his backline – Spain only conceded one goal in their eight matches at the tournament. Rodri completed 756 passes (more than anyone at the tournament) and he also topped the charts for touches, line-breaking passes and passes in the opposition third. In the final alone he completed 101 passes, completely strangling the life out of Argentina to the extent that they did not have a single shot on target.

He lifted the trophy as Spain’s captain, won the Golden Ball as the tournament’s best player and earned a place in one of football’s most exclusive clubs as only the fourth man in history to have won the World Cup, European Championship, European Cup and Ballon d’Or, joining Gerd Müller, Franz Beckenbauer and Zinedine Zidane.

Kylian Mbappé

Kylian Mbappé went toe-to-toe with his old Paris Saint-Germain teammate Lionel Messi at the World Cup. They battled it out for the trophy, the Golden Boot, the Golden Ball and a place in the history books as the competition’s all-time leading scorer. He won two of the four. His two goals in the third-place playoff against England ensured he became the first man to win the Golden Boot twice. It also brought him to 22 goals in World Cups – one more than Messi – and made him the first man to reach double figures in a single edition since Müller in 1970.

And yet, it was not what Mbappé wanted. “I would have preferred not to be the top scorer and to have played in the final,” said the France captain. His domestic season was also prolific but disappointing, bringing goals and individual glory but no silverware. He scored 42 goals in 44 appearances, finishing the season as the top scorer in La Liga and the Champions League, but he did not win either trophy. The goals flowed but the medals did not follow. As Kane has discovered, goals alone are rarely enough to win the Ballon d’Or.

View image in fullscreen Kylian Mbappé has scored 22 goals in 22 matches at World Cups. Photograph: Carlos Barría/Reuters

Lionel Messi

Lionel Messi sat on the floor alone in a stadium of 80,000 people, boots off, staring into the distance as Spain’s substitutes streamed past him in celebration. It was not the fairytale image the Argentina captain had envisioned as he left the world stage. And, given his performances over the previous six weeks, it felt as if he deserved better even if his team did not.

Some expected Messi’s tournament to be a nostalgia act – a former great wheeled out for one last World Cup as he prepares for his 40th birthday. But then he went and scored a hat-trick in Argentina’s first game. He scored twice against Austria, then added another against Jordan. He stamped his authority on the tournament in the group stage and proceeded to drag Argentina through the knockouts: a goal against Cape Verde, a goal and an assist against Egypt, an assist against Switzerland, and two more assists to sink England in the semi-final. Had it not been for Mbappé’s brace in a bizarre third-place playoff, he would have collected the Golden Boot.

Could he win the Ballon d’Or having lost the World Cup final? In only four of the last 19 years has the award gone to a player who did not win the Champions League, World Cup, European Championship or Copa América in the same year. But three of them were won by Messi. A ninth Ballon d’Or is unlikely but the fact he is in this conversation at all – at 39 while playing in MLS having lost a final – is testament to his greatness.

This is an article by WhoScored

Sports.title: Franco Baresi was not only the captain but the moral heart of great Milan team
Sports.content:
There are very few players who become bywords for their position, who enjoy universal acclaim. But for anybody who watched football in the late 80s or early 90s, Franco Baresi was the central defender. He was unsurpassed, obviously the best in his position in the world, the definition of the art of the defending. The oddity is, he really wasn’t like very many other defenders at all.

Baresi had just turned 19 when he won his first scudetto at Milan under Nils Liedholm. It was 1979 and Italian football was still dominated by the ideals of catenaccio. Most defences comprised a libero, two man-markers and, if you were lucky, an attacking left-back. But not Liedholm’s. The Swede was a pioneer in Serie A of zonal marking, and the idea that the game was not a series of physical battles but a question of space. Baresi was only 5ft 9in and a teenager. More traditional coaches might not have trusted him. But Liedholm saw an impeccable reader of the game, even at that age. Baresi was an ever-present, not only in the league but in the Coppa Italia and Uefa Cup as well.

That turned out to be a traumatic season for the club, with players arrested on the pitch after the final game of the season as part of the Totonero betting scandal, for which Milan were ultimately relegated. With the club in financial chaos, promotion was followed by another relegation and, although they were promoted again, the future seemed bleak before Silvio Berlusconi took over in 1986. Baresi remained loyal throughout. His parents died before he turned 16 and Milan became a sort of surrogate family.

He never played for any other club, amassing 719 appearances in all competitions over 20 years. And yet, he could easily have been an Inter player. Baresi’s brother Giuseppe, two years his elder, was already at Inter when Franco was offered a trial at the age of 14. Inter wondered if he was big enough to make it and asked him to come back the following year. So Franco went for a trial at Milan – which he insisted had always been his club – and was taken on.

Berlusconi was an outsider, determined to disrupt the establishment. In Arrigo Sacchi, who was appointed in 1987, he found a coach in the same vein: a radical who followed Liedholm’s tentative steps into the world of zonal marking with a giant leap into a full-blown flat back four and hard pressing. In the Serie A of the age it was almost unthinkably revolutionary. Conservatives were sceptical and, when Milan lost their second game of the season 2-0 at home to Fiorentina, and followed that up with defeat to Espanyol in the Uefa Cup and a disappointing draw against Cesena, the joke was that Berlusconi’s new messiah would not make All Saints’ Day, which is 1 November.

Form began to turn around, but Sacchi worried he had pushed the players too hard and eased back on training, at which point Baresi made a decisive intervention. He begged Sacchi to push the players even harder. It was vital, he said, that the players didn’t forget, that they came to learn the new way of playing, of working out their position not according to preset formulas but through constantly evolving reference to opponents, their teammates, the ball and the space, to internalise the processes until they became instinctive.

View image in fullscreen Franco Baresi (kneeling, second left) and his Milan teammates celebrate beating Steaua Bucharest 4-0 to win the 1989 European Cup, for many the high point of their football under Arrigo Sacchi. Photograph: PA Images/Alamy

For Sacchi, it was a huge moment. Baresi was not only the captain, but the moral heart of the team. If he was on board with the revolution, Sacchi realised, the squad would follow. Milan, with their ultra-modern style, won the scudetto in 1988 and backed it up with consecutive European Cup wins, playing some of the most memorable football ever witnessed. Baresi was central to it, not only snuffing out opposing forwards but constantly analysing and organising, and also initiating counterattacks. The clipped forward pass became a trademark, but his greatest skill was his pass selection. He just didn’t give the ball away.

His inspirations were creative players plus Ruud Krol, but Baresi was also tough. Gianfranco Zola called him the best defender he ever played against but observed that afterwards “your feet need loads of ice and anti‑inflammatories”. Baresi dished it out, as defenders in Serie A in those days had to, but he could also take it. He played more than an hour of a Milan derby in 1989 with a broken arm, helping keep a clean sheet, and, at the 1994 World Cup, managed to recover from knee surgery required after tearing his cartilage in the second group game in time to play in the final. Again, he oversaw a clean sheet but, cruelly, failed from the spot in the shootout as Italy lost to Brazil.
