World.title: Liberia: Boakai Purges Senior Security Officials Across Multiple Agencies
World.content:
President Joseph Nyuma Boakai has dismissed or suspended senior officials at Roberts International Airport, the Liberia National Police, the National Security Agency, the Liberia Drug Enforcement Agency and the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection over the country's two record cocaine seizures, and ordered that those implicated be turned over for prosecution.

The action, announced Thursday by the Executive Mansion, is the widest personnel purge of the investigation so far and reaches into every institution that touched the shipments.

Among those dismissed is Mark Egon Kuiah, deputy director for operations at Roberts International Airport. His removal came a day after the president's son, Joseph Nyuma Boakai Jr., devoted part of a public statement to a friendship with a man he named as Mark Kuiah, describing him as a friend of many years who he had never had reason to believe was anything but law-abiding, and adding that friendship is not immunity from the law.

Also dismissed were Johnny Bolar Dean, the police commissioner for criminal investigation, intelligence and Interpol, and Patrick Doe, deputy director for administration at the National Security Agency. Dean had already been removed from his post last week after admitting he took US$10,000 to provide comfort to two suspects held in the airport case.



The president recalled and suspended without pay Patrick Komasu, an NSA agent seconded to the LDEA, and placed him under investigation.

Boakai ordered the dismissal of all government and law enforcement employees implicated in the cases. Those named include the airport's security director, Mohammed O. Gbowrah, and LDEA deputy commander Moses Jallah, both stationed at Roberts International Airport.

Two police officers were dismissed over the use of official vehicles to move narcotics. The Executive Mansion named them as Anthony T. Blaye and Wadell W. Kwarbo, and said they moved a consignment from Vincent Town on the Bomi Highway to the vicinity of Mega Mart in Thinker Village, Paynesville.

That account sits alongside, and does not obviously match, the one Inspector General Gregory Coleman gave reporters hours earlier, in which the two men were said to have escorted narcotics from a landing site to a holding ground with police vehicles running ahead of and behind the load. Coleman did not name the route.

Four others were ordered dismissed and turned over to the Ministry of Justice for prosecution: NSA agents Jammel V. Jallah, Christian L. Nyantee and Albenigo Janior, and Caycee Nelson, procurement director at the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection.

The Executive Mansion said the removals are meant to hold public servants to account. "These actions demonstrate his Administration's resolve to ensure that no public official or government employee who engages in criminal conduct remains in public service," the release said.

Close 

Boakai said the law would be enforced without fear or favor, directed security institutions to press the investigations further, and said everyone connected to the cases must go before the courts with due process observed.

The announcement followed the public destruction earlier Thursday of the cocaine recovered in both cases. The government put the Duazon haul at US$317 million and the June 8 airport seizure at US$19 million, a combined US$336 million, and said the two hauls together came to 4,169 plates.

World.title: Uganda: HIV Injection Is Not a Vaccine, Experts Warn
World.content:
Kampala — Experts have urged those who already received their first injection of the twice-yearly HIV preventing drug Lenacapavir to consider using combination prevention options, warning that the game changer injection is not a vaccine.

The initial recipients of the drug that has since had a lot of demand countrywide are set to receive their second dose in October and Dr Vincent Bagambe, the Policy Planning and Strategic Manager at the Uganda AIDS Commission says for those who access it, they should be keen on receiving their next dose on the prescribed dates if they are to maintain optimal drug levels in their blood.

Bagambe says that with the injection now part of the prevention tools in the country, they hope to cut the 37,000 new infections recorded yearly to less than 10,000 by 2030, which will all depend on how compliant people be to maintain the required drug levels in their blood to guarantee protection.

At the launch of the prevention option in April, Uganda had received 19,200 doses supplied across 103 health facilities across the country. The main clients targeted for the drug include people at highest risk of infection such as sex workers, couples in discordant relationships, fisherfolk and pregnant women engaging in risky behavior among others. But reports by the Ministry of Health show that the drug was accessed by those not listed as high risk as demand surpassed available supplies.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Asked about supplies for those who will soon need the second dose, Dr Herbert Kadama who coordinates Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) at the Ministry of Health said sixty - percent of the facilities that received the first batch have now received second batches.

Kadama explains that the facilities received the second batches earlier than scheduled because the doses were running out in two to three weeks and yet at the beginning, they had thought they would be supplying every two months.

Meanwhile, the country expects a top-up consignment of another 19,200 doses donation.

In an earlier interview with URN, Dr Peter Mudiope who heads HIV Prevention in the ministry this consignment was initially expected to arrive in the country in June only to be informed by the manufacturer Gilead Sciences that this couldn't happen due to shortages of a tablet that complements the injection, also called the loading dose.

Mudiope says that as calls for more doses continue and the valid need for people to comply on the prevention treatment, government cannot do much to avail the game changer drug for now. He says the current price of Lenacapivir is still too high to be afforded by the government. At 28,000 dollars per dose, the official says Uganda can for now only count on more donations expected from Global Fund and the American government to guarantee availability.

Close 

With supplies not yet guaranteed, Mudiope says the public should continue relying on other prevention options such as condoms, Pre and Post Exposure Prophylaxis tablets and being faithful as they are equally scientifically tested and confirmed to prevent HIV infection.

However, a study conducted by Makerere University School of Public Health in which they assessed access to HIV prevention services found use of key prevention options low.

According to results of this study which were released on Wednesday, researchers found only 24 percent of female sex workers and injection drug users, who are also a high at-risk group used PEP in the last three months. Seventy-six percent reported to have not used the prevention option despite knowledge of where to access it.

In terms prevalence, while national prevalence currently stands at 4.9 percent, among sex workers and injection drug users, HIV prevalence is high at 30 percent and 17 percent respectively.

Ideally, Kadama says such groups are the ones targeted as a top priority for Lenacapavir.

World.title: East Africa: U.S. Senators Urge Rubio to Address Impact of Ebola Outbreak on Women
World.content:
press release

WASHINGTON — Yesterday, U.S. Senators Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Ranking Member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, and Lisa Murkowski (R-AK) sent a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio urging the State Department to take swift action to protect women and infants from the deadly impact of the Ebola outbreak in eastern Africa. The Senators called on the Trump Administration to promptly use congressionally appropriated funds for voluntary family planning programming to distribute already purchased family planning commodities and back the UN Population Fund’s (UNFPA) health clinics operating in the region.

In the letter, the Senators emphasized the catastrophic toll of Ebola on pregnant women and warned that conflict and displacement in Ituri and North Kivu—in addition to increases in gender-based and sexual violence and transactional and survival sex—are exacerbating the outbreak.

“Ebola during pregnancy is catastrophic, with a nearly 100 percent fetal loss rate and catastrophic maternal mortality risk due to severe hemorrhaging. By providing women with the option to voluntarily prevent unplanned pregnancies and to protect themselves from transmission of the virus and have access to clinics, the United States can prevent further deaths of women and the cruel and certain death of any fetus exposed to the virus,” wrote the Senators.

“The inclusion of family planning in the U.S. response to the Ebola virus, including condoms and hormonal contraceptive methods, post-rape care and lifesaving anti-hemorrhage maternal health medicines is paramount. Congress, on a bipartisan basis, supports voluntary family planning programs because such programs support families and reduce maternal and infant death rates. In East Africa right now, access to family planning is essential to protecting women and babies and to reducing viral transmission,” continued the Senators.



“The rapid spread of the virus, with more than 2,000 confirmed cases and 796 confirmed deaths as of this week in the DRC, leaves no time for delay in providing all possible interventions to save lives and prevent the transmission of the virus. The cost of United States response is approaching $1 billion. Investment now in voluntary family planning is fiscally rational in addition to being morally urgent,” concluded the Senators.

Full text of the letter is available HERE and provided below.

Dear Secretary Rubio,

We write to urge the State Department to take swift action to address the devastating impact of the Ebola outbreak in eastern Africa on women and infants by utilizing funding provided by Congress for voluntary family planning programming, to distribute already purchased family planning commodities and supporting the UN Population Fund’s (UNFPA) health clinics in the region.

Ebola during pregnancy is catastrophic, with a nearly 100 percent fetal loss rate and catastrophic material mortality risk due to severe hemorrhaging. By providing women with the option to voluntarily prevent unplanned pregnancies and to protect themselves from transmission of the virus and have access to clinics, the United States can prevent further deaths of women and the cruel and certain death of any fetus exposed to the virus.

During the Ebola outbreak in West Africa from 2014-2016, maternal mortality rose an estimated 75%. The staggering increase in maternal mortality was a result of the Ebola virus, as well as pregnant women forgoing antenatal and attended delivery care because of fear of contracting the virus at health clinics.

Currently, conflict and displacement are exacerbating the Ebola outbreak with spikes in gender-based and sexual violence in Ituri and North Kivu, as well as an increase in transactional and survival sex. Access to voluntary family planning counseling and supplies is critical to protect the lives of women and babies and to control the spread of the virus.

The inclusion of family planning in the U.S. response to the Ebola virus, including condoms and hormonal contraceptive methods, post-rape care and lifesaving anti-hemorrhage maternal health medicines is paramount. Congress, on a bipartisan basis, supports voluntary family planning programs because such programs support families and reduce maternal and infant death rates. In East Africa right now, access to family planning is essential to protecting women and babies and to reducing viral transmission. We urge you to utilize the $608 million in international family planning funding included in the Fiscal Year 2026 Appropriations bill and to distribute the remaining $1.7 million in already purchased family planning commodities in storage in Geel, Belgium which we understand will otherwise be destroyed.

Close 

We also ask that you issue a humanitarian exemption to support UNFPA's sexual and reproductive health programming in affected areas. UNFPA is already operational across 29 health zones in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and in Uganda; emergency contributions would be deployed immediately through an existing, proven delivery system with no ramp-up delay. Providing sexual and reproductive health support to women is not a parallel track alongside the Ebola response: it is the Ebola response for the 642,000 women of reproductive age - including an estimated 37,820 pregnant women - in the affected areas.

The rapid spread of the virus, with more than 2,000 confirmed cases and 796 confirmed deaths as of this week in the DRC, leaves no time for delay in providing all possible interventions to save lives and prevent the transmission of the virus. The cost of United States response is approaching $1 billion. Investment now in voluntary family planning is fiscally rational in addition to being morally urgent.

World.title: Nigeria: South African Singer Tyla Cancels Lagos Performance Amid Xenophobia Backlash
World.content:
South African singer Tyla has removed Lagos from the schedule of her upcoming APop world tour following online backlash from some Nigerians over renewed reports of xenophobic attacks against Nigerians in South Africa.

The Grammy-winning artiste unveiled the dates for her world tour on Monday, with the initial itinerary including a Lagos concert scheduled for December 22, alongside stops across Europe, North America and South Africa.

However, the announcement sparked heated reactions on Nigerian social media, where several users questioned the decision to host the singer amid reports of fresh xenophobic violence targeting Nigerians in South Africa.



The controversy revived long-standing tensions between both countries, with some social media users calling for a boycott of the Lagos concert.

Others argued that entertainment should not be linked to diplomatic disputes and maintained that musicians should not be held responsible for political or societal conflicts.

A number of public figures also weighed in on the debate.

Media personality Do2dtun questioned the promoters behind the planned Lagos show, while activist and former presidential candidate Omoyele Sowore urged Nigerians to channel their frustrations toward political leaders rather than the artiste.

Neither Tyla nor her management publicly addressed the criticism.

However, checks by VANGUARD showed that Lagos has been removed from the list of tour venues on the official ticketing platform.

The previously announced December 22 show in Nigeria no longer appears among the available dates.

The updated schedule now lists only the remaining international stops, including performances across Europe, North America and two South African shows in Cape Town on January 4 and Johannesburg on January 9.

Tyla has not announced whether the Lagos concert was cancelled permanently or if it could be rescheduled at a later date.

World.title: Ghana: Govt Backs Five-Year Presidential Term
World.content:
The government has accepted the recommendation of the Constitutional Review Committee (CRC) to extend the term of office of the President from four to five years, with the tenure of Parliament adjusted accordingly.

The Attorney-General and Minister for Justice, Dr Dominic Akurutinga Ayine, said the move was aimed at providing administrations with more time to plan, implement and assess policies.

"Under the current four-year cycle, the early months of every administration are consumed by transition, and the final year is lost to elections. A five-year term provides a more realistic timeframe for policy formulation, implementation and assessment," he explained.

Dr Ayine made this known at the Presidency in Accra yesterday when he presented the government's position paper on the recommendations of the CRC.



Related Articles

He said, subject to approval through a referendum, the government also supported a fixed single, non-renewable 10-year term for the Chief Justice, up to the mandatory retirement age of 70 years.

He added that the government had proposed capping the number of Supreme Court justices at 19, comprising the Chief Justice and 18 other justices.

"The Committee recommended a cap of 15 justices; government proposes 19 justices; Chief Justice plus 18 Justices of the Supreme Court. This promotes efficiency, manages public expenditure, while remaining sufficiently robust to discharge the Court's constitutional mandate," he said.

Dr Ayine, who is also the Member of Parliament for Bolgatanga East, said Ghanaians were expected to vote in a referendum next year on the proposed amendments to the 1992 Constitution.

The referendum, he explained, would be held alongside the District Assembly elections to allow citizens to endorse or reject the government's position on the recommendations of the Prof. Henry Kwesi Prempeh-led committee.

The CRC report, titled "Transforming from Electoral Democracy to a Developmental Democracy," was presented to President John Dramani Mahama in February 2026, after which three Cabinet retreats were held before government arrived at its position.

Among the other recommendations considered were presidential election dates, election petitions, presidential taxation, the minimum age for presidential candidates, the size of government and Parliament.

On the minimum age for the Presidency, Dr Ayine said although the committee recommended 30 years, the government's position was that it should be raised to 35 years.

"Thirty-five is consistent with modern democratic constitutions towards greater inclusivity of youth, whilst ensuring candidates have maturity and experience," he said.

He said government had also accepted the proposal for presidential elections to be held in the first week of November, arguing that a fixed date would provide certainty in the electoral calendar and allow sufficient time between elections and the January 7 inauguration.

Dr Ayine said government supported a constitutional requirement for presidential election petitions to be filed within 14 days after the declaration of results and determined by the Supreme Court within 30 days.

He added that the Electoral Commission would be required to provide relevant electoral data to the court and all parties involved in the hearing.

On presidential taxation, the Attorney-General said government had accepted in principle that the President should pay taxes on salary, allowances and applicable direct taxes on bills and services. However, taxes on presidential retirement gratuity and pension would remain exempt.

Close 

On the size of government, Dr Ayine said while the CRC recommended a maximum of 57 ministers, government proposed an upper limit of 60.

He added that ministers could either be appointed from Parliament or outside it.

Regarding Parliament, he said the legislature would be capped at 300 members, with an additional 24 seats created through proportional representation for women, persons with disabilities and the youth.

Dr Ayine further disclosed that dual citizens by birth would no longer be barred from contesting parliamentary elections solely because of their dual citizenship.

"Multiple citizenship will no longer disqualify a person from holding specified offices, except that of President and Vice President," he stated.

He also announced that District Chief Executives would be elected, with the President nominating five persons including two women from whom three candidates would be shortlisted for election.

World.title: Tanzania: President Unveils Roadmap to New Constitution
World.content:
Dar es Salaam — PRESIDENT Samia Suluhu Hassan announced yesterday that the government will establish a reconciliation commission to facilitate the next phase of the constitutional review process, reaffirming her administration commitment to political dialogue and national unity.

The Head of State made the remarks at State House in Dar es Salaam during a meeting with leaders of the country's 18 registered political parties, where discussions centred on political reconciliation, constitutional reforms, economic development, employment, investment and the preservation of peace.

President Samia said the proposed reconciliation commission would help accelerate consensus building ahead of constitutional reforms while ensuring that all processes are conducted in accordance with the country's laws, regulations and established procedures.



"We already want to form a reconciliation commission to expedite the process of the Constitution or constitutional amendments," President Samia said.

She stressed that safeguarding Tanzania's peace, unity and national resources is a shared responsibility that extends beyond the government to political parties and all citizens.

"The responsibility of protecting Tanzania belongs to all of us. Democracy is about participating in elections, accepting the outcome and allowing the winner to form the government. But protecting our country and the blessings God has given us is the duty of every Tanzanian," she said.

The President called on political parties to continue working together with the government in preserving national peace and stability, noting that democracy thrives where there is shared responsibility and collective commitment to the country's prosperity.

"Democracy is about shared prosperity and shared responsibility before success. The government may be formed by the winning party, but the benefits of development belong to all Tanzanians," she said.

President Samia also reaffirmed the government's commitment to sustaining political reconciliation efforts, saying consultations with political parties would continue regularly as part of efforts to strengthen democracy and inclusive governance.

She announced that the government would continue convening meetings with leaders of political parties at least three times a year to discuss issues of national importance.

The meeting was the second of its kind convened by President Samia since the 2025 General Election.

The first meeting was held on March 31 this year, bringing together presidential candidates and their running mates who contested the election.

Referring to reconciliation efforts in Zanzibar, the President briefed party leaders on the progress made in preparations for the next phase of political reconciliation, which will pave the way for constitutional review.

Close 

She assured participants that every stage of the process would be guided by the law and undertaken in the broader national interest.

On the economy, President Samia said Tanzania maintained strong economic performance, with the economy growing by six per cent last year and projected to expand by 6.3 per cent this year.

She said the government remains focused on completing ongoing strategic development projects while continuing investments in key infrastructure, including railways, roads, ports and other major facilities.

The President noted that improvements at the Dar es Salaam Port have significantly enhanced its capacity to serve domestic and regional trade, adding that expansion works are also continuing at ports along the Indian Ocean as well as Lakes Victoria, Tanganyika and Nyasa.

Political party leaders also presented their views on governance, economic growth, social development and citizens' welfare.

The government pledged to continue receiving and considering their recommendations through established dialogue platforms and formal decision-making mechanisms.

World.title: Nigeria: Opposition PDP Submits Goodluck Jonathan's Presidential Candidacy
World.content:
Abuja — The Kabiru Turaki-led Interim National Working Committee of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, on Friday said it had manually submitted former President Goodluck Jonathan's presidential nomination and the names of its other candidates for the 2027 general elections to the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, despite the electoral body's refusal to recognise the committee.

The move deepens the party's leadership crisis, with the Turaki camp insisting it validly nominated its candidates in line with the Electoral Act and warning of fresh legal action if INEC publishes a different list.

Addressing journalists, the committee's National Publicity Secretary, Comrade Ini Ememobong, said the party opted for manual submission after INEC declined to provide access codes for electronic submission, insisting the codes were only an administrative convenience.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

"Notwithstanding INEC's refusal to provide us with the necessary access codes... we have successfully submitted, manually and in full compliance with the Electoral Act 2026, the list of candidates sponsored by the authentic Peoples Democratic Party," Ememobong said.

He added that the submission, which included Jonathan's presidential nomination and all governorship, National Assembly and state assembly candidates, was acknowledged by INEC.

Ememobong warned the commission against publishing any list other than the one submitted by the committee.

"Should the Commission publish names other than those lawfully submitted by us... we are exhausting every constitutional, legal and democratic avenue to ensure that our party is not hijacked or annexed to the ruling party," he said.

He traced the dispute to the Supreme Court judgment on the PDP's leadership, saying the party's Board of Trustees and a requisitioned National Executive Committee meeting constituted the Interim National Working Committee after the ruling left the party without a legally recognised national leadership.

According to him, INEC declined to recognise the interim leadership despite being formally notified, forcing the party to seek judicial intervention.

Faulting the Federal High Court judgment, Ememobong said, "The judgment... reads more like an appeal on the judgment of the Supreme Court and the Court of Appeal. It is clearly inconsistent with the extant decisions of the Supreme Court and the Court of Appeal that form the foundation of our case."

He said the party had appealed the judgment and would also challenge alleged discrepancies between the judgment delivered in court and the Certified True Copy.

The PDP also accused INEC of abandoning its neutrality.

"The Commission's actions have regrettably reinforced the growing public perception that it is no longer acting with the impartiality expected of the nation's electoral umpire," Ememobong said.

Close 

He alleged that the commission withheld material facts in court proceedings involving the party and ignored congresses it monitored, warning that such actions were eroding public confidence in the electoral process.

Ememobong further alleged that the PDP was the first target of a broader campaign to weaken opposition parties and entrench one-party dominance.

"We were the pioneer target for opposition dismantling and capture... but it has now spread to almost all the opposition parties," he said.

Calling on Nigerians to defend multi-party democracy, Ememobong warned that electoral authoritarianism undermines democratic consolidation before expressing confidence that the party would prevail.

World.title: Nigeria: Resident Doctors Threaten Nationwide Strike
World.content:
NARD said the proposed Total and Comprehensive Industrial Strike (TICS) would commence at 8 a.m. on 10 August unless its demands are met before the deadline.

The Nigerian Association of Resident Doctors (NARD) has threatened to embark on a nationwide indefinite strike from 10 August if the federal government fails to address outstanding salary arrears, welfare concerns and other longstanding issues affecting its members.

The association announced the decision in a communiqué issued after its National Executive Council (NEC) meeting in Gombe State, where it reviewed the implementation of previous agreements reached with the government.

NARD said the proposed Total and Comprehensive Industrial Strike (TICS) would commence at 8 a.m. on 10 August unless its demands are met before the deadline.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

"The NEC reaffirmed its commitment to constructive engagement and dialogue but reiterated that the welfare of resident doctors and the survival of Nigeria's healthcare system remain non-negotiable," the communiqué stated.

Unpaid arrears

Among its demands, the association called for the immediate payment of outstanding arrears arising from the 25 and 35 per cent Consolidated Medical Salary Structure (CONMESS) review, 19 months of unpaid professional allowance arrears, as well as outstanding salary and promotion arrears owed to doctors in several federal health institutions.

It also urged the government to ensure that all eligible resident doctors omitted from the 2026 Medical Residency Training Fund (MRTF) disbursement are paid without further delay.

While acknowledging the federal government's recent disbursement of the residency training fund to eligible beneficiaries, NARD said many financial obligations to resident doctors remain unresolved.

LUTH crisis

The association also raised concerns over what it described as the continued intimidation of resident doctors at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH).

It accused the hospital management of refusing to provide call duty meals despite repeated engagements and called on the federal government to intervene.

NARD warned that failure to resolve the issues at LUTH before 10 August would leave it with no option but to proceed with industrial action.

Assaults on doctors, broader healthcare challenges

NARD condemned what it described as persistent assaults, harassment and intimidation of doctors across the country, saying such incidents threaten an already fragile healthcare system.

It called for a national protocol to prevent violence against healthcare workers and urged lawmakers to criminalise assaults on health personnel.

The association expressed concern over deteriorating infrastructure in public hospitals, citing inadequate medical equipment, unreliable electricity supply and poor maintenance of health facilities.

It also highlighted chronic underfunding of the health sector, shortages of healthcare workers and high out-of-pocket healthcare costs, saying these continue to limit access to quality healthcare for millions of Nigerians.

NARD urged federal and state governments to increase investment in healthcare, strengthen primary healthcare services, improve health financing and recruit more health workers to advance universal health coverage.

The association further called for the speedy conclusion and implementation of the Medical and Health Workers' Collective Bargaining Agreement and the recommendations of the ministerial committee reviewing excessive workloads, prolonged call duty hours, casualisation of doctors and the abuse of locum appointments.

Close 

It also demanded urgent action to address salary delays, unpaid arrears and internship placement challenges affecting house officers.

Nigeria has experienced several industrial actions by resident doctors in recent years, with disputes largely centred on unpaid salaries and allowances, poor working conditions, residency training funding and the implementation of agreements reached with the government.

Health experts have repeatedly warned that prolonged strikes disrupt access to healthcare, delay surgeries and worsen pressure on an already overstretched health system, particularly for patients who rely on public hospitals.

World.title: How much longer does Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney realistically have in Death Valley?
World.content:
If I were to ask you to describe Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney in one word, your response would likely hinge almost entirely on how far back your memory goes when it comes to watching college football.

If you’re fairly new to the sport, you would probably use words like "washed" or "cooked" or even "fired" given his performance relative to expectations since the turn of the decade.

Fans who have been around for a while longer and know why those expectations exist at Clemson would opt to use words like "legend" or "champion."

'HOT SEAT RANKINGS' FOR ALL 16 SEC COACHES AS BEGINNING OF 2026 COLLEGE FOOTBALL SEASON DRAWS NEARER

However, if you’re an older college football fan and happen to remember the Tigers pre Dabo, you’d use words like "god" or "untouchable."

This is because you would be painfully aware of where Clemson was as a program in the years leading up to Swinney's arrival.

Sure, the Tigers have a national championship from the early 80s, but outside of that, no one was counting Clemson as a blue blood in the three decades before Dabo donned the tiger paw-crested polo.

CURT CIGNETTI REVEALS HOW WORKING FOR NICK SABAN CHANGED EVERYTHING: 'EVERY DAY WAS 4TH-AND-1'

From 1990-2008, the Tigers finished a season ranked inside the AP top-10 just once, as coaches like Tommy West and Tommy Bowden produced middling results year after year.

Enter Swinney, who, after becoming the full-time coach in 2009, has a robust 180-47 record, seven AP top-ten finishes, a remarkable nine ACC championships, and two national titles to his name.

All of that is to say, Dabo Swinney is Clemson football.

THREE INTRIGUING QUARTERBACK BATTLES TO WATCH DURING COLLEGE FOOTBALL OFFSEASON CAMPS

But after a disappointing 2025 season in which the Tigers went from top-five preseason Playoff darlings to Pinstripe Bowl losers, is the clock ticking for the winningest coach in ACC football history?

It's been well documented that Swinney is rather resistant to change in the world of college football, particularly when it comes to NIL and the transfer portal, both of which are seen as essential to competing in today's day and age.

You could make the argument that Dabo's unwillingness to embrace modernity has put Clemson a step behind the elites of college football, but the Tigers just won an ACC Championship and were in the College Football Playoff two years ago.

The question then becomes, is that good enough?

Is getting an invite to the dance but never being dangerous enough to win the whole thing acceptable now that Swinney himself has ratcheted up the expectations in western South Carolina?

That remains to be seen. The natives are restless, but as far as I (or anyone else, for that matter) can tell, leadership doesn't seem to be in a big rush to show Dabo the door.

That brings us to this coming season.

What will 2026 look like for the Tigers and what is a "safe" year for Swinney?

Contrary to what they showed last season, I think Clemson will have a big bounce back year this season.

As long as they get the quarterback decision right (and that's a big "if"), the Tigers have weapons like TJ Moore and Bryant Wesco Jr. to field a dynamic offense.

We talked about Swinney's affinity for familiarity in the face of change, so he will likely be thrilled to see an old friend in Chad Morris back on the headset as Clemson's offensive coordinator.

Morris was the OC for the Tigers from 2011-2014, which is right around the time the program started ascending, so maybe a familiar face from the glory days is just what Dabo needs to right the ship.

There is talent to be found all over this roster, but that's never been the issue.

I think Swinney and the Tigers will relish in the fact that no one is talking about them this offseason.

Leading up to the 2025 season, Clemson and Swinney were expected to compete for a national title, and they crumbled beneath the weight of their own goals.

This year's squad is similarly talented, but will be flying under the radar, and that could be a blessing.

The schedule is a mixed bag, though, as the Tigers open up with their fellow striped-cat brethren in LSU.

Outside of that game and a home contest against Miami, though, the slate for 2026 looks more than manageable.

Clemson will be the more talented team in almost all of their match ups, save for the two aforementioned games against LSU and Miami, so 9-3 or 10-2 is absolutely within reach.

That kind of year would easily buy Swinney some more time, but based on everything we've discussed, I'm not sure he even needs it.

Never say never, but I truly believe Dabo Swinney has the closest thing to a "lifetime contract" at Clemson that you'll see in modern sports.

Swinney has done everything he can to turn the Tigers into a traditional power in college football, so when the time comes for Dabo to call it quits, he will likely be doing so on his own schedule.

I don't know if Clemson will ever achieve the heights they reached in the 2010s with Swinney at the helm again.

For now, eight to ten wins and an occasional CFP berth might be the ceiling until Swinney decides to call it quits.

Or maybe the pendulum swings back the other direction with regard to NIL and the transfer portal, and Dabo looks like a genius playing the long game.

Either way, Dabo Swinney likely isn't going anywhere, this year or beyond.

It will be a long time before another coach like him comes along.

World.title: The biggest threat in America's race with China isn't Beijing, tech executive warns
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

America's biggest obstacle in the technology race with China may no be Beijing, but growing resistance to new data centers and the power needed to run them, according to Palantir's chief technology officer.

"The proximate issues are definitely going to be power and backlash against data centers," Shyam Sankar said in an interview with Fox News Digital at Palantir's American Builder Summit.

Sankar, whose company builds software for the Pentagon, intelligence agencies and major manufacturers, argued the U.S. risks slowing its own technological progress more than falling behind Beijing.

"The only threat to AI generating prosperity for America is suicide, not homicide."

The U.S. and China are pouring billions into the race to dominate artificial intelligence, viewing the technology as central to economic growth, military power and geopolitical influence. Winning that race depends on an enormous buildout of data centers, power generation and transmission infrastructure to support increasingly capable systems. But those projects have drawn growing resistance from communities worried about electricity demand, water use and whether the benefits will outweigh the costs.

LEADING ECONOMIST WARNS OF RISE OF 'GEN Z AFFORDABILITY SOCIALISM'

Companies have raced to build new data centers to support a wave of new computing infrastructure, fueling a nationwide expansion that has also sparked growing local opposition. The issue has spilled into the 2026 midterm campaigns, with candidates in battleground states such as Pennsylvania running ads focused on the economic and environmental effects of the projects.

Residents have raised concerns about electricity demand, water consumption, noise, traffic and whether utility customers will ultimately bear the cost of expanding the power grid. Some projects have been delayed or canceled, while lawmakers in several states have proposed restrictions or moratoriums on new facilities.

THE WAR ON DATA CENTERS JEOPARDIZES OUR ECONOMY AND NATIONAL SECURITY

Some developers have responded by pairing new data centers with dedicated power generation rather than relying entirely on the electric grid.

Sankar argues those debates risk slowing the industrial gains the technology can already deliver. He pointed to one submarine-parts manufacturer that cut production planning from two weeks to less than an hour, freeing enough capacity to add a third shift.

"There is no one on that shift who thinks, 'Hey, I got my job because of AI,' but that's actually what happened," he said.

The summit itself appeared designed to counter one of the AI industry's biggest public relations challenges: fears that the technology will replace jobs. Rather than showcasing increasingly capable AI models, Palantir filled the stage with factory workers, healthcare workers and military personnel demonstrating software they had built to solve problems in their own workplaces.

Sankar argued the AI industry has become overly focused on pursuing artificial general intelligence, or AGI, rather than deploying today's AI systems across the economy.

Artificial general intelligence, or AGI, refers to a still-theoretical system capable of performing a broad range of intellectual tasks at or beyond human level, rather than excelling mainly at narrower tasks such as writing, coding or image analysis.

He compared the current moment to the early days of electricity, arguing that while the technology already exists, businesses have yet to reorganize themselves around it.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"The AI we have is powerful enough that it should have created more prosperity and value," he said. "The only reason it hasn't yet is not a failing of the technology, it's a lack of our national will to push and invest in diffusing the technology through our economy."

"We shouldn't lose the plot in pining away for a machine god," he added.

The summit brought together a cohort of Palantir's American Tech Fellowship, where workers from industries including manufacturing, healthcare and defense demonstrated AI applications they had built for use in their jobs.

The demonstrations were intended to illustrate Sankar's contention: that AI will make workers more productive than ever rather than replace them.

That runs against much of the public sentiment, where workers across industries have begun to wonder how long until their jobs will be done by a machine.

FOX NEWS POLL: MOVE OVER BIG BROTHER, VOTERS SEE BIG TECH AS GREATER THREAT TO US

"How many people have actually, at the front line, have experienced AI and how it's changed their job versus how many people are imbibing the fear-mongering from the social media feed, which is partially a Chinese Psyop as well."

World.title: Planned Parenthood across Midwest at risk due to lack of federal funds after 3 facilities close in Michigan
World.content:

Planned Parenthood of Michigan (PPMI) announced Thursday that it is permanently closing three health centers across the state, pointing to a sharp decline in federal funding and Medicaid reimbursement restrictions pushed by national Republicans.

The organization will close facilities in Lansing, Livonia and Warren. None of the three locations provided procedural abortions.

"Republicans in Congress have now demonstrated that they are willing to block Medicaid reimbursement for Planned Parenthood patients, and the Trump administration has proposed eliminating the Title X family planning program altogether," Planned Parenthood of Michigan President and CEO Paula Thornton Greear said in a statement.

COALITION OF 25 STATES SUES TRUMP ADMIN OVER MEDICAID WORK RULE DESIGNED TO PREVENT FRAUD

According to the organization, the closures follow a $4.2 million drop in patient care reimbursements and federal family planning grants compared to the previous fiscal year. Additionally, the affiliate reported carrying an unsustainable $5.6 million in uncompensated and undercompensated care.

PPMI said the decision came after a comprehensive evaluation of its statewide network, following earlier cost-cutting measures that included eliminating administrative and non-clinical roles to prioritize direct patient care.

Planned Parenthood officials warned that reproductive health care providers across the Midwest face similar financial strains due to chronic underfunding, shifting state and federal Medicaid rules, and rising operational costs.

Susan B. Anthony Pro-Life America’s Director of State Affairs Sue Liebel told Fox News Digital, "Michiganders deserve far better than Planned Parenthood for their hard-earned tax dollars. Not only is Planned Parenthood America’s biggest killer of babies in the womb , it is also known for botching procedures , killing or severely injuring women and girls in Michigan and nationwide."

"All three of the closed facilities exclusively sold dangerous abortion drugs, which are a more profitable method for the abortion industry, but have been found to inflict serious adverse effects like hemorrhage, infection and sepsis in as many as 11% of women who take them," Liebel added. "For every Planned Parenthood facility in Michigan, there are at least 20 community health centers offering women’s healthcare that are ready to welcome and truly serve low-income and other patients."

EXCLUSIVE: PENCE WARNS GOP 'MUST DELIVER,' OR PLANNED PARENTHOOD GETS TAXPAYER CASH ON FOURTH OF JULY DEADLINE

Thornton Greear signaled potential restructuring earlier this year after federal policy changes restricted Planned Parenthood’s Medicaid eligibility and Title X allocations.

"We have to reshape how we deliver care so Planned Parenthood of Michigan can continue serving patients for generations to come," Thornton Greear said. "That means concentrating our resources at regional access points and procedural sites and continuing to expand virtual care across Michigan. These are painful decisions, but they are strategic decisions grounded in where we can preserve access for the greatest number of patients."

The closures stem from federal legislation signed into law last year that restricts federal funds — including Medicaid reimbursements — from going to organizations that perform abortions. Under the provision, Medicaid reimbursements are barred for providers that receive more than $800,000 in Medicaid funds and offer certain abortion services.

EXCLUSIVE: PLANNED PARENTHOOD SET FOR MASSIVE TAXPAYER WINDFALL IF SENATE FAILS TO ACT

While federal law has long prohibited taxpayer dollars from directly funding abortion services in most cases under the Hyde Amendment, Planned Parenthood leaders argue the newer restrictions target their broader family planning and preventive health operations.

In February, Planned Parenthood voluntarily dismissed its lawsuit challenging the administration's Medicaid funding restriction. Despite the legal setback, organization leaders pledged to consolidate services into regional hubs and expand telehealth offerings statewide.

World.title: Navy SEAL and survival show host Joel Lambert warns Americans to prepare for weeks without supplies
World.content:
Former Navy SEAL and Discovery Channel host Joel Lambert says Americans preparing for an emergency should forget the Hollywood fantasy of grabbing a backpack and disappearing into the wilderness.

Instead, they should start by making sure they can survive inside their own homes.

Lambert, author of "A Navy SEAL’s Bug-In Guide: How to Turn Your House into the Safest Place on Earth," joined OutKick’s "Tomi Lahren is Fearless" this week to discuss emergency preparedness, wilderness survival and what television survival shows get right — and wrong.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK

While Lambert said he is optimistic about humanity’s future, he also warned that getting there could involve serious uncertainty.

"I think we’re heading toward a brave new world in a good way," Lambert said. "I think we’re in the fourth turning, and we’re moving into a golden age in the world and humanity. However, that’s going to be a bumpy ride."

That makes self-sufficiency especially important, he said, whether the disruption comes from war, political instability, a natural disaster or a widespread power outage.

Lambert’s advice is not built around one miracle tool or expensive piece of tactical gear. He said families should instead prepare for a scenario in which ordinary services and supplies are unavailable for an extended period.

"I think you need to be prepared for a, say, six-to-eight-week scenario where you’re not able to get prescriptions," Lambert said. "You’re not able to get medications. You’re not able to get grocery store runs, or they might be limited, or water issues or power issues."

That means having enough essentials to get every member of the household through several weeks without relying on a last-minute grocery run.

And sure, six to eight weeks of emergency supplies might sound a little alarmist — maybe borderline doomsday prep-y. But you don’t have to be staring down Armageddon or nuclear annihilation for those supplies to come in handy.

A hurricane, major snowstorm, flood or city-wide power outage can disrupt access to food, clean water, medication, electricity or cell service. These things happen all the time.

Lambert grouped human needs into five basic categories: shelter, water, food, communication and navigation.

"Shelter, water, food, which are the most important in that order, and then communications and navigation," he said.

Communication could include anything that allows a person to receive or transmit information, from a cell phone to a signal fire. Navigation means having the ability to travel safely and know where you are even when modern technology or infrastructure is unavailable.

The key, Lambert said, is to prepare before an emergency arrives.

"Get your house in order," he said. "Make sure that you have some food to get yourself through, you know, several weeks of uncertainty."

Lambert also offered a reality check for viewers who think watching survival television has prepared them for the real thing.

He described CBS’ "Survivor" as more of an elimination competition than a true survival program and acknowledged that even legitimate outdoor shows must make concessions for television production.

Lambert hosted Discovery’s "Lone Target," also released internationally as "Manhunt," which followed him as he attempted to evade military and law-enforcement tracking units in remote environments.

"When I started doing survival shows on Discovery Channel, I did not want to be a fake survival show," Lambert said. "I’m like, I just got out of the SEAL team. So I’m like, ‘if I’m going to do this, I’m gonna do it real.’"

Some high-risk portions, such as parachute jumps, were filmed separately so an injury would not derail an entire production. Lambert said the actual pursuits, however, were genuine.

"Everything that happened from the time I inserted ‘til the time I got extracted was real," he said.

He recalled an episode filmed in Africa in which he continued moving through an area where lions were hunting, despite the crew attempting to stop him.

Lambert said he encountered lions that had recently made a kill and realized he "could really literally die in the African bush doing the show."

Still, he continued.

"It’s better to finish and die than quit and live," Lambert said.

Spoken like a true Navy SEAL.

Fortunately, the average person is far more likely to face a power outage, storm or water disruption than a team of trackers and hungry lions.

For ordinary wilderness situations, Lambert recommended remembering the "rule of threes." A person can generally survive approximately three hours without shelter in harsh conditions, three days without water and three weeks without food.

That order matters.

"Everyone always tends to go to food immediately, just because that’s what we all think of, but you can go a long time without food," Lambert said.

Asked whether someone should drink directly from a creek or another natural water source, Lambert said the circumstances will always dictate the decision. But whenever possible, the water should be purified.

"In the wild, you always need to purify your water just ’cause you just don’t know," he said. "You can find the most beautiful mountain stream that’s just clear and perfect, and you don’t know a mile up there’s a dead buck or something laying in the middle of the stream."

WOULD THIS SURVIVAL POD MAKE YOU FEEL SAFER?

Lambert recommended carrying a portable filtration straw or hand pump, along with iodine or chlorine tablets. Those inexpensive tools can dramatically reduce the risk of becoming sick from contaminated water.

Fire is another versatile survival tool. Given a choice between hunting equipment, a tarp or a ferro rod in a tropical jungle, Lambert said he would likely choose the ability to make fire.

"Fire is shelter," he said. "It protects your corporeal body from the elements. You can purify water, you can cook food, you can signal with fire, you keep warm."

The lesson running through Lambert’s advice is that survival is rarely about possessing one flashy item or a singular strategy. The environment, weather and immediate threat should determine the next move.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

But for most Americans, Lambert explained, the first move is much simpler. Build a reserve of food, clean water, necessary medication and basic emergency equipment before you need them.

Because when the alarms are already blaring, it may be too late to start getting the house in order.

World.title: Sophie Cunningham fan who was confronted by Storm co-owner opens up on incident and facing trans athletes
World.content:
Washington state high school athlete Ahnaleigh Wilson was pushed into a starting spot under the lights of the national culture war over women's sports this week when she was allegedly berated at a WNBA game.

Now, in an exclusive interview with Fox News Digital, she and her family are speaking out for the first time since Seattle Storm co-owner Celeste Keaton was suspended for an exchange with the teenager.

Wilson went viral Tuesday night for speaking out about being allegedly heckled by Keaton during the Storm's game against the Indiana Fever. Wilson was not prepared to take on such public attention, and she and her family say it has caused them issues. The teen was there simply to support Sophie Cunningham after Cunningham took a public stand to save girls' sports.

"She was sitting directly across from us on the court, and we hadn't really noticed her much. And then she had walked over to talk to the people to the right of where we were sitting, and when she stopped talking to them, she turned and looked at us," Wilson, who sat courtside, told Fox News Digital.

STORM CO-OWNER SUSPENDED AFTER INCIDENT WITH SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM FANS AS STAR BREAKS SILENCE ON CONTROVERSY

Keaton then allegedly called Wilson and her friend "f—ing insane," for her support of Cunningham and the protection of women's sports.

"After she was done, she kind of just walked away, and me and my friend were just like, 'What just happened?' Um, we were kind of stunned. I was like, "I'm not gonna cry, not gonna cry." Um, but I feel like I kind of cry, I don't know, when I feel overwhelmed or anything, honestly. So I started crying a little, and I was kind of embarrassed, 'cause I really didn't want to," Wilson added.

The emotional response was in part because of how personal the issue of protecting girls' sports is for Wilson. Washington is one of the 19 states in the U.S. that actively protects the rights of males to compete in girls' sports. So in eighth grade, she and her family said she lost a regional championship race to a biological male trans athlete in May 2024.

Wilson had to work her way back from a knee injury to compete in that race, and had the lead, up until the final lap, before the trans athlete zoomed past her and took first place. Wilson also said she had to compete against a male athlete four times this past school year in cross country.

"They don't know my story. They don't know that I've actually experienced this, and I've experienced it more than once. I'm going to junior year now, and I've competed against a biological male four times. these people don't even know what I've gone through," she said.

"It's disappointing, especially when it's other women."

So when Cunningham publicly took a stand for protecting girls' sports, it was enough to motivate Wilson to go to a WNBA game for the first time. She attended a rally outside Climate Pledge Arena in celebration of Cunningham.

But when Wilson got inside Climate Pledge Arena, she says she was heckled by other fans and eventually by Keaton, which brought her to tears, then spoke about the experience in a since-viral interview right after the game with independent Washington-based journalist Brandi Kruse.

When Wilson woke up the next morning, she slowly realized what she had gotten into.

Her friend opened Instagram first. One post about the incident appeared, followed by another. Then came coverage from national outlets. By the time the WNBA announced Keaton’s punishment, the story was everywhere.

"It was crazy," Wilson said. "I was expecting it, obviously, to kind of be big because it is a WNBA co-owner of the Seattle Storm and she was rude, but I guess I wasn’t expecting it to blow up that quick."

"It was pretty shocking. A little overwhelming, but also I was glad that the WNBA did something about it."

Her father, Brendan Wilson, said the family knew Ahnaleigh’s courtside sign might attract some attention. They expected a photograph of her supporting Cunningham to circulate. They did not anticipate their daughter becoming the face of a national WNBA controversy.

"She was going there with the intention of supporting Sophie and glad that somebody of Sophie’s stature was supporting Ahnaleigh," Brendan said. "She kind of expected her picture might be somewhere, that she was sitting courtside with a sign in support, but nothing of this magnitude at all."

The attention quickly spread beyond news reports about Keaton. Strangers found photographs of Wilson and began directing insults at the teenager and her family.

"Our daughter’s face is plastered everywhere," her mother, Elizabeth Wilson, said. "We are getting comments of hate. A lot of support, though, too, but this has exploded, and her actions have now impacted our family greatly and will continue to do so."

Wilson said she has tried to avoid reading the responses. The messages she has seen have accused her of being a bigot, transphobic and anti-trans. One commenter dismissed her as a "stupid white girl," she said.

"If you know me, you know I’m not any of those things and that I do care about people," Wilson said. "I’m okay with people being different and being different from me."

Wilson said her family has LGBTQ friends and relatives. She said her position is focused on the competitive consequences of allowing biological males into girls’ sports, not hostility toward transgender people.

"Those people don’t know me, and they don’t know that I love everyone," she said. "I don’t have an issue with people being trans. It’s just that it’s unfair when it comes to sports."

Elizabeth said the family has leaned on its Christian faith while trying to process the national attention.

"It’s overwhelming," she said. "We’re trying to continue to be Christ-like and trying not to be so angry and hateful. It’s definitely been a balance of trying to balance our feelings and just trying to let God lead us exactly where he needs us to go."

The Storm issued a public apology after the encounter became national news.

"We are aware one of our co-owners made comments to two fans in attendance at last night’s game," Storm majority owner Ginny Gilder said. "We apologize that this happened. Everyone who attends a Storm game deserves to feel welcome, and we remain committed to creating an inclusive environment where every fan is treated with respect."

The WNBA later confirmed to Fox News Digital that Keaton was fined and suspended from attending Seattle’s next five home games.

The Wilson family said it appreciated the speed of the league’s response but believes the Storm and Keaton still owe the girls a personal apology. They said no one from the team or the WNBA has reached out to them since the incident.

"They owe these girls an apology," Elizabeth said. "She needs to be held accountable. We teach our kids that every choice has a consequence, good or bad, and you have to own up to your mistakes."

Elizabeth also alleged Keaton’s actions made other spectators feel emboldened to target the teenagers.

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM RALLY ROCKS WNBA GAME AS 'SAVE WOMEN'S SPORTS' ACTIVISTS FACE COUNTER-PROTEST

"By her coming up to them and verbally attacking them and bullying them into putting their signs away, she opened that up for the people around them to treat the other girls and our daughter and her friend in a similar manner," Elizabeth said. "She allowed that to happen."

The family also wants greater transparency about Keaton’s punishment.

"I’m glad that they took accountability, but five games and then they’re going to fine her, which is probably a drop in the hat, means, like, nothing," Elizabeth said. "We would just be interested to know: How much are they fining her? Where is that fine going?"

Brendan said he appreciates how quickly the league acted to suspend Keaton.

"I was glad that they didn’t waste much time in showing everybody that that kind of behavior is unacceptable and suspending her," he said. "This incident with our daughter, at least, was handled from the WNBA quickly, and we appreciate that."

But Elizabeth is still hoping for a personal outreach from the WNBA.

"We definitely would like to see them do something more personal, like reach out to our family personally and apologize for what happened," she said. "I think that’s a necessary step that hasn’t happened."

Fox News Digital reached out to the Storm for a response to the Wilson family’s statements.

The public attention was a burden for the family when it first began to pile up on Tuesday night and Wednesday morning. But their spirits improved as the day went on after the Storm apologized and news of Keaton's suspension came out.

But the most rewarding part came late on Wednesday night.

Ahnaleigh and her friend were playing pool when Elizabeth came downstairs and told them Cunningham had posted about them.

"We were all jumping up and down," Elizabeth said.

Cunningham wrote that she believed there was "a safe space and love for EVERYBODY," including biological girls and boys, transgender women and transgender men.

"Everyone is welcome at my table," Cunningham wrote. "You can disagree and still be kind. Bravo to those girls for standing up for what they believe."

Cunningham promised the teenagers gifts and called the conduct attributed to Keaton "truly embarrassing."

Wilson and her friend stopped playing pool and pulled up the post.

"We were shocked," Wilson said. "It was just insane. It was a super cool moment. It was cool to see her acknowledge us."

The family said it would welcome the opportunity to attend another Fever game. It does not expect to return to a Storm game, even if Keaton or the organization eventually apologizes.

"We can’t support an organization like that," the family said.

"We would love to go see the Fever play again," Elizabeth added. "But I don’t think we’d go back to Seattle to watch them play."
